board_events.text: Diathermic (conducting) wall: heat passes through
Adiabatic (insulating) wall: heat blocked entirely
Thermal interaction depends entirely on the wall

segments.text: <curious>What is warmth, really? You cannot see it, weigh it, or bottle it. Thermodynamics is the physics of heat and temperature, and it studies them from a deliberately zoomed-out point of view.
It is a macroscopic science. We do not track every molecule zipping around inside a gas. Instead we ask which few bulk numbers ordinary instruments can grab directly.
That handful is pressure, volume, temperature, mass, and composition. Bundle them together and you have what we call the thermodynamic state of the system.
A system is simply the chunk of the universe we choose to study, such as the gas in a cylinder. Everything outside it is the surroundings, and the boundary between them is the wall.
Here is the quiet hero of the whole story: the wall. Its type decides whether two systems can feel each other thermally at all.
A diathermic, or conducting, wall lets heat flow through. Two gases separated by a diathermic wall keep exchanging energy until they settle.
An adiabatic, or insulating, wall blocks heat completely. Each side lives in its own world, oblivious to the other.
So whether two systems interact thermally depends entirely on the wall between them. Hold on to that idea; the next law is built on it.
<curious>Warmth असल में है क्या? आप इसे देख नहीं सकते, तौल नहीं सकते। Thermodynamics heat और temperature की physics है, और यह इन्हें एक zoomed-out नज़रिए से देखती है।
यह एक macroscopic science है। हम gas के अंदर हर molecule को track नहीं करते। बजाय इसके, हम पूछते हैं कि कौन से थोड़े से bulk numbers हमारे instruments सीधे माप सकते हैं।
वो थोड़े से numbers हैं pressure, volume, temperature, mass, और composition. इन्हें साथ में bundle करो, तो यही कहलाता है system का thermodynamic state.
System बस universe का वो हिस्सा है जिसे हम study करना choose करते हैं, जैसे cylinder में भरी gas. उसके बाहर सब कुछ है surroundings, और दोनों के बीच की boundary है the wall.
यहाँ है पूरी कहानी का quiet hero: the wall. इसका type तय करता है कि दो systems thermally एक दूसरे को feel कर सकती हैं या नहीं।
एक diathermic, यानी conducting wall, heat को अपने through बहने देती है। इस wall से अलग की गई दो gases तब तक energy exchange करती हैं जब तक settle नहीं हो जातीं।
एक adiabatic, यानी insulating wall, heat को पूरी तरह block कर देती है। हर side अपनी अलग दुनिया में रहती है, दूसरे से बेखबर।
तो दो systems thermally interact करेंगी या नहीं, यह पूरी तरह उनके बीच की wall पर depend करता है। इस idea को पकड़ के रखो; अगला law इसी पर बना है।

board_events.text: Equilibrium is transitive, like an equals sign
Zeroth Law: A with C and B with C imply A with B
Equal-in-equilibrium number = temperature
Discovered last, numbered first: it births temperature
Equal temperature is NOT equal energy

segments.text: Picture two friends in adjoining train compartments. Open the connecting door and they chat until every piece of gossip is shared, reaching a settled state where nothing more changes.
For two systems in thermal contact, that settled state is thermal equilibrium: the hot one cools, the cold one warms, and their macroscopic variables stop drifting.
Now the quietly profound part. Put A in equilibrium with C, and B separately in equilibrium with the same C, while A and B stay insulated from each other.
Remove the insulation between A and B, and nothing changes. They were already in equilibrium. Thermal equilibrium is transitive, exactly like an equals sign in algebra.
That single observation is the Zeroth Law: if A and B are each in thermal equilibrium with C, then A and B are in equilibrium with each other.
And it does something beautiful. It guarantees every system carries a single number that is equal exactly when two systems are in equilibrium. We name that number temperature.
So temperature is not assumed at the start. It is forced into existence by the zeroth law. That is why this law, discovered last, is numbered first.
One guardrail. The zeroth law promises equal temperature at equilibrium; it says nothing about equal energy. Two systems at the same temperature can hold wildly different internal energy.
सोचो, दो दोस्त बगल-बगल के train compartments में हैं। बीच का दरवाज़ा खोल दो, तो वे तब तक बातें करते हैं जब तक हर gossip share न हो जाए, एक settled state तक जहाँ अब कुछ नहीं बदलता।
thermal contact में रखी दो systems के लिए वो settled state है thermal equilibrium: गरम वाली ठंडी होती है, ठंडी वाली गरम, और उनके macroscopic variables बदलना रुक जाते हैं।
अब आता है वो गहरा हिस्सा। A को C के साथ equilibrium में रखो, और B को अलग से उसी C के साथ, जबकि A और B एक दूसरे से insulated रहें।
A और B के बीच का insulation हटाओ, और कुछ नहीं बदलता। वे पहले से ही equilibrium में थीं। Thermal equilibrium transitive है, बिलकुल algebra के equals sign की तरह।
यही एक observation है the Zeroth Law: अगर A और B दोनों अलग-अलग C के साथ thermal equilibrium में हैं, तो A और B आपस में भी equilibrium में हैं।
और यह एक खूबसूरत काम करता है। यह guarantee करता है कि हर system एक single number रखती है, जो तभी equal होता है जब दो systems equilibrium में हों। उस number को हम कहते हैं temperature.
तो temperature शुरू में मान नहीं ली जाती। इसे zeroth law अस्तित्व में लाता है। इसीलिए यह law, जो सबसे बाद में discover हुआ, number में सबसे पहले है।
एक guardrail. Zeroth law equilibrium पर equal temperature का वादा करता है; equal energy का नहीं। एक ही temperature की दो systems बहुत अलग-अलग internal energy रख सकती हैं।

board_events.text: 4. The shared label = temperature
5. A thermometer compares without direct contact
Every thermometer reading rests on transitivity
An empirical law whose power is logical

segments.text: This is the reasoning chain that examiners at the top tier love. Follow each link, because temperature itself hangs from it.
Link one, observation. Join two systems by a diathermic wall, and their macroscopic variables change and then stop. We call that unchanging condition thermal equilibrium.
Link two, the experiment. Put A and B each in equilibrium with a third body C, keeping A and B insulated. Remove the insulation, and nothing changes. That is the zeroth law as a raw fact.
Link three, partition. Being in equilibrium with C sorts all systems into groups, where every member is in equilibrium with every other. Each group needs a label.
Link four, the label. Assign each group a number that two systems share if and only if they are in mutual equilibrium. That number is temperature, now legitimate by construction.
<whisper>Link five, the payoff. Because of this, you never press two objects together to compare them. You touch a thermometer to each in turn; equal readings guarantee equal temperature.
Every temperature measurement you have ever made silently relies on this chain. The thermometer works only because equilibrium is transitive.
There is no algebra to memorise here. The zeroth law is empirical; its power is entirely in this logic that brings temperature into being.
यह वो reasoning chain है जो top-tier examiners को बहुत पसंद है। हर link को follow करो, क्योंकि temperature खुद इसी पर टिकी है।
Link एक, observation. दो systems को diathermic wall से जोड़ो, तो उनके macroscopic variables बदलते हैं और फिर रुक जाते हैं। इस unchanging condition को हम thermal equilibrium कहते हैं।
Link दो, experiment. A और B को अलग-अलग एक तीसरी body C के साथ equilibrium में रखो, A और B insulated रखते हुए। insulation हटाओ, कुछ नहीं बदलता। यही zeroth law एक raw fact की तरह है।
Link तीन, partition. C के साथ equilibrium होना सारी systems को groups में बाँट देता है, जहाँ हर member हर दूसरे के साथ equilibrium में है। हर group को एक label चाहिए।
Link चार, label. हर group को एक number दो जो दो systems तभी share करें जब वे आपस में equilibrium में हों। वही number है temperature, अब construction से ही legitimate.

<whisper>Link पाँच, payoff. इसी वजह से आप कभी दो चीज़ों को compare करने के लिए आपस में नहीं दबाते। आप बारी-बारी हर एक को thermometer से छूते हैं; equal readings equal temperature की guarantee देती हैं।
आपने जितनी भी temperature माप ली है, वो चुपचाप इसी chain पर टिकी है। Thermometer सिर्फ़ इसलिए काम करता है क्योंकि equilibrium transitive है।
यहाँ रटने के लिए कोई algebra नहीं है। Zeroth law empirical है; इसकी ताक़त पूरी तरह इसी logic में है जो temperature को अस्तित्व में लाती है।

segments.text: With temperature in hand, we can write the equations that pin a state down. Here is the toolkit for this subtopic.
For an ideal gas the state is tied together by the equation of state: P V equals n R T. Pressure times volume equals moles times the gas constant times absolute temperature.
Here P is pressure, V is volume, n the number of moles, T the absolute temperature in kelvin, and R the universal gas constant.
A per-molecule form uses the Boltzmann constant: P V equals capital N times k B times T, where capital N is the number of molecules.

Memorise the constants: R is eight point three one four joules per mole per kelvin, k B is one point three eight times ten to the minus twenty three, and the triple point of water is two hundred seventy three point one six kelvin.
The zeroth law, stated formally, gives temperature: if T of A equals T of C and T of B equals T of C, then T of A equals T of B.
Two classifications matter. Cut the system in half: whatever stays the same is intensive; whatever halves is extensive.
State variables such as P, V, T, and U depend only on the current state. Path variables, heat Q and work W, depend on the route taken and are meaningless as a stored amount.
अब जब temperature हाथ में है, हम वो equations लिख सकते हैं जो state को pin करती हैं। यह रहा इस subtopic का toolkit.
ideal gas के लिए state को equation of state जोड़ती है: P V equals n R T. Pressure into volume बराबर है moles into gas constant into absolute temperature.
यहाँ P है pressure, V है volume, n है moles की संख्या, T है absolute temperature kelvin में, और R है universal gas constant.
एक per-molecule form Boltzmann constant use करती है: P V equals capital N into k B into T, जहाँ capital N molecules की संख्या है।

constants याद रखो: R है eight point three one four joules per mole per kelvin, k B है one point three eight into ten to the minus twenty-three, और water का triple point है two hundred seventy-three point one six kelvin.
zeroth law, formally कहें तो temperature देता है: अगर T of A बराबर T of C और T of B बराबर T of C, तो T of A बराबर T of B.
दो classifications मायने रखती हैं। System को आधा काटो: जो same रहे वो intensive; जो आधा हो जाए वो extensive.
State variables जैसे P, V, T, और U सिर्फ़ current state पर depend करते हैं। Path variables, heat Q और work W, चले गए रास्ते पर depend करते हैं और stored amount के रूप में meaningless हैं।

board_events.text: (i) $P$ with $R$ and (ii) equal temperature: both correct
(iii) equal internal energy: the trap ($U$ extensive)
Answer: (i) and (ii) only

segments.text: Two quick examples. The first is a clean plug-in; the second is a favourite one-line trap.

Board level. A rigid cylinder holds an ideal gas at volume zero point zero two five cubic metres, pressure two point zero times ten to the fifth pascals, and temperature three hundred kelvin. Find the moles.

Rearrange the equation of state for n. It is P V over R T, which is two point zero times ten to the fifth, times zero point zero two five, all over eight point three one four times three hundred, about two point zero moles.
Notice pascals times cubic metres equals joules, which cancel cleanly against the joules in R, leaving moles. Checking the units is the fastest sanity check in the exam hall.
Now the speed trap. Three sealed flasks: P is in equilibrium with Q, and Q with R. A student draws three conclusions.
Conclusion one: P is in equilibrium with R. Conclusion two: all three share one temperature. Both are just the zeroth law applied, so both are correct.

<whisper>Conclusion three, equal internal energy, is the trap. Temperature is intensive, but internal energy is extensive; a flask with five moles holds far more than one with a single mole at the same temperature.
The moment a question offers an equal-energy option beside equal-temperature, suspect the energy option. Equal T is what the zeroth law gives; equal U it never promises.
दो जल्दी examples. पहला एक clean plug-in है; दूसरा एक favourite one-line trap है।

Board level. एक rigid cylinder में ideal gas है volume zero point zero two five cubic metres, pressure two point zero into ten to the fifth pascals, और temperature three hundred kelvin पर। moles निकालो।

equation of state को n के लिए rearrange करो। यह है P V over R T, यानी two point zero into ten to the fifth, into zero point zero two five, बटा eight point three one four into three hundred, लगभग two point zero moles.
ध्यान दो, pascals into cubic metres बराबर joules, जो R के joules के against cleanly cancel हो जाते हैं, moles छोड़ते हुए। units check करना exam hall में सबसे तेज़ sanity check है।
अब speed trap. तीन sealed flasks: P, Q के साथ equilibrium में है, और Q, R के साथ। एक student तीन conclusions निकालता है।
Conclusion एक: P, R के साथ equilibrium में है। Conclusion दो: तीनों एक temperature share करते हैं। दोनों बस zeroth law का application हैं, तो दोनों सही हैं।
<whisper>Conclusion तीन, equal internal energy, ही trap है। Temperature intensive है, पर internal energy extensive; पाँच moles वाली flask उसी temperature पर एक mole वाली से कहीं ज़्यादा रखती है।
जिस पल कोई question equal-temperature के साथ equal-energy का option देता है, energy option पर शक करो। Equal T zeroth law देता है; equal U वो कभी वादा नहीं करता।

board_events.text: Fixed partition, insulated box: total internal energy conserved
One temperature now, but two separate volumes
Equilibrium fixes T, not P: different moles, same volume

segments.text: A rigid, externally insulated container is split by a fixed conducting partition. Two different gas samples share heat until they settle.
The left half holds two point zero moles of a monoatomic gas at four hundred kelvin; the right half three point zero moles of the same gas at three hundred kelvin.
First ask what is conserved. The partition is fixed, so no work is done, and the container is insulated, so no heat leaves. Total internal energy is constant.
For a monoatomic ideal gas, internal energy is three halves n R T. Setting the total before equal to the total after, the three-halves R cancels from every term.
So the final temperature is the mole-weighted mean: two times four hundred plus three times three hundred, all over five, which is seventeen hundred over five, equal to three hundred forty kelvin.
By the zeroth law this single temperature now describes both halves. Each half still keeps its own fixed volume, so we can now find each pressure separately.
Using P equals n R T over V for each side gives about five point six five times ten to the fifth pascals on the left, and about eight point four eight times ten to the fifth on the right.
The temperatures equalise, but the pressures do not. Thermal equilibrium fixes temperature, never the other state variables, because the halves hold different amounts of gas in the same volume.
एक rigid, externally insulated container एक fixed conducting partition से बँटा है। दो अलग gas samples तब तक heat share करते हैं जब तक settle न हो जाएँ।
बाँयी half में two point zero moles monoatomic gas है four hundred kelvin पर; दाँयी half में three point zero moles वही gas three hundred kelvin पर।
पहले पूछो क्या conserve हो रहा है। partition fixed है, तो कोई work नहीं होता, और container insulated है, तो कोई heat बाहर नहीं जाती। Total internal energy constant है।
monoatomic ideal gas के लिए internal energy है three halves n R T. पहले का total बाद के total के बराबर रखो, तो three-halves R हर term से cancel हो जाता है।
तो final temperature mole-weighted mean है: two into four hundred plus three into three hundred, बटा five, यानी seventeen hundred over five, बराबर three hundred forty kelvin.
zeroth law से यह एक temperature अब दोनों halves को describe करती है। हर half अपना fixed volume रखती है, तो अब हम हर pressure अलग निकाल सकते हैं।
हर side के लिए P equals n R T over V लगाने पर बाँयी तरफ़ लगभग five point six five into ten to the fifth pascals, और दाँयी तरफ़ लगभग eight point four eight into ten to the fifth.
temperatures बराबर हो जाती हैं, पर pressures नहीं। thermal equilibrium temperature fix करती है, बाक़ी state variables कभी नहीं, क्योंकि halves एक ही volume में अलग-अलग gas रखती हैं।

board_events.text: Both final readings must be equal: the thermometer is system three
Heat lost = heat gained: mass-weighted mean
Qualitative answer first, value second: it leans toward the heavier bath

segments.text: An advanced problem where the zeroth law hands you the qualitative answer before you touch a single calculation.
A constant-volume gas thermometer reads one point one zero P-tr in bath A and one point three zero P-tr in bath B. Bath A is two kilograms of water, bath B one kilogram.

Convert the readings to temperature with T equals two hundred seventy three point one six times P over P-tr. Bath A is about three hundred point five kelvin; bath B about three hundred fifty five point one.

<curious>Now the deep move. When A and B reach mutual equilibrium they share one temperature. The thermometer is itself a third system, so it must register the same value in each. The two final readings are identical, before any arithmetic.
Only now do the masses set the number. Heat lost equals heat gained, which gives the mass-weighted mean of the two starting temperatures.
That mean is two times three hundred point five plus one times three hundred fifty five point one, all over three, about three hundred eighteen point seven kelvin.
Convert back to a reading: P-final equals P-tr times three hundred eighteen point seven over two hundred seventy three point one six, about one point one seven P-tr in each bath.
The zeroth law gave the qualitative answer, equal readings, before any calculation. The masses only fixed the value, and it sits nearer bath A exactly as the two-to-one mass ratio demands.
एक advanced problem जहाँ zeroth law आपको qualitative answer एक भी calculation छूने से पहले दे देता है।
एक constant-volume gas thermometer bath A में one point one zero P-tr और bath B में one point three zero P-tr पढ़ता है। Bath A है two kilograms पानी, bath B एक kilogram.
readings को temperature में बदलो T equals two hundred seventy-three point one six into P over P-tr से। Bath A लगभग three hundred point five kelvin; bath B लगभग three hundred fifty-five point one.

<curious>अब गहरी चाल। जब A और B आपस में equilibrium तक पहुँचती हैं, वे एक temperature share करती हैं। thermometer खुद एक तीसरा system है, तो उसे हर एक में same value दिखानी होगी। दोनों final readings identical हैं, किसी arithmetic से पहले।
अब जाकर masses number तय करती हैं। heat lost बराबर heat gained, जो दोनों starting temperatures का mass-weighted mean देता है।
वो mean है two into three hundred point five plus one into three hundred fifty-five point one, बटा three, लगभग three hundred eighteen point seven kelvin.
reading में वापस बदलो: P-final equals P-tr into three hundred eighteen point seven over two hundred seventy-three point one six, हर bath में लगभग one point one seven P-tr.
zeroth law ने qualitative answer, equal readings, किसी calculation से पहले दे दिया। masses ने सिर्फ़ value तय की, और वो bath A के पास है, जैसा two-to-one mass ratio माँगता है।

sections.subtopic: Thermodynamic State and the Zeroth Law
sections.title: Common pitfalls and pro-tips

board_events.text: Four pitfalls, then two speed habits
1. Equal temperature is not equal energy
2. Only two of P, V, T are independent
3. Heat is not stored: Q and W are path quantities
4. The gas law needs kelvin, never Celsius
Ratio form: cancel the constant, get a one-line proportion
Write equal final T first, then compute

segments.text: Four traps sink more students here than anywhere else in this topic. Let us disarm each.
Pitfall one, and the biggest. Confusing equal temperature with equal energy. A tiny hot system and a huge warm system can hold the same energy; two same-temperature systems usually do not.
Pitfall two. Treating P, V, and T as three independent variables. They are bound by P V equals n R T, so for a fixed mass only two are free; specifying all three over-determines the state.
Pitfall three. Calling heat a state variable. Q and W are path quantities; only P, V, T, and U are point functions. Never write the heat content of a gas.
Pitfall four. Using temperature in degrees Celsius inside the gas law. The equation demands kelvin, always. Convert by adding two hundred seventy three point one five.
First speed habit. For a fixed amount of the same gas between two states, use the ratio form P-one V-one over T-one equals P-two V-two over T-two, and cancel whatever is held constant.
Second habit. For any two-bodies-reach-equilibrium question, write the qualitative answer, equal final temperature, before touching the algebra. It anchors the whole solution.
चार traps इस topic में और कहीं से ज़्यादा students को डुबोते हैं। हर एक को disarm करते हैं।
Pitfall एक, और सबसे बड़ा। equal temperature को equal energy समझ लेना। एक छोटी गरम system और एक बड़ी गुनगुनी system same energy रख सकती हैं; एक ही temperature की दो systems आमतौर पर नहीं।
Pitfall दो। P, V, और T को तीन independent variables मान लेना। वे P V equals n R T से बँधे हैं, तो fixed mass के लिए सिर्फ़ दो free हैं; तीनों बताना state को over-determine कर देता है।
Pitfall तीन। heat को state variable कहना। Q और W path quantities हैं; सिर्फ़ P, V, T, और U point functions हैं। कभी gas का heat content मत लिखो।
Pitfall चार। gas law के अंदर temperature को degrees Celsius में डालना। equation kelvin माँगती है, हमेशा। two hundred seventy-three point one five जोड़ के convert करो।
पहली speed habit। एक ही gas के fixed amount के लिए दो states के बीच, ratio form P-one V-one over T-one equals P-two V-two over T-two use करो, और जो constant है उसे cancel कर दो।
दूसरी habit। किसी भी two-bodies-reach-equilibrium question में, qualitative answer, equal final temperature, algebra छूने से पहले लिख दो। यह पूरे solution को anchor करता है।

board_events.text: Door one: heat Q crosses because of a temperature difference
Door two: work W as the piston moves
$\Delta Q = \Delta U + \Delta W$
Income = change in savings + spending
Conservation of energy, wearing a gas costume
First law balances energy but predicts no direction

segments.text: <curious>We know a gas owns a genuine state variable, its internal energy. The natural next question is the one this whole law answers: how can that owned energy change?
Picture a fixed amount of gas trapped under a frictionless, movable piston. This is the single most important mental image in all of thermodynamics.
There are exactly two doors through which energy can enter or leave this gas. Only two, and there is no third.
Door one is heat. Place the cylinder on a hot stove, and because of the temperature difference, energy seeps in as heat Q.
Door two is work. Push the piston in and you cram energy into the gas; let the gas push the piston out and it spends energy doing work on the surroundings.
The first law is honest accounting of these two doors: change in heat equals change in internal energy plus the work done. Read it as a sentence.
Treat the gas like a bank account. Heat is the salary credited, work is the rent paid out, and the change in internal energy is the change in your balance.
Nobody invents money from nothing, and no gas invents energy from nothing. That is simply conservation of energy, written for a gas.

But note its blind spot. The first law is a bookkeeper, not a fortune-teller. It guarantees energy balances, yet says nothing about which direction a process goes. That gap is what the second law fills.
<curious>हम जानते हैं कि gas एक असली state variable रखती है, उसकी internal energy. अगला natural सवाल वही है जिसका यह पूरा law जवाब देता है: वो owned energy बदल कैसे सकती है?
सोचो, एक fixed amount gas एक frictionless, movable piston के नीचे बंद है। यह पूरी thermodynamics की सबसे ज़रूरी mental image है।
इस gas में energy आने-जाने के ठीक दो दरवाज़े हैं। सिर्फ़ दो, और कोई तीसरा नहीं।
दरवाज़ा एक है heat. cylinder को गरम चूल्हे पर रखो, और temperature difference की वजह से energy heat Q बनकर अंदर रिसती है।
दरवाज़ा दो है work. piston को अंदर धकेलो और आप gas में energy भर देते हो; gas को piston बाहर धकेलने दो और वो surroundings पर work करके energy खर्च करती है।
first law इन दो दरवाज़ों का ईमानदार हिसाब है: change in heat बराबर change in internal energy plus किया गया work. इसे एक वाक्य की तरह पढ़ो।
gas को एक bank account मानो। heat है credit हुई salary, work है चुकाया गया rent, और internal energy का change है आपके balance का change.
कोई पैसा शून्य से नहीं बनाता, और कोई gas energy शून्य से नहीं बनाती। यह बस conservation of energy है, gas के लिए लिखा हुआ।
पर इसका blind spot देखो। first law एक bookkeeper है, fortune-teller नहीं। यह energy balance की guarantee देता है, पर यह नहीं बताता कि process किस direction जाएगी। वो gap second law भरता है।

board_events.text: Change in $U$ depends only on the endpoints
$\Delta Q - \Delta W$ is path-independent
Over a closed cycle the change in $U$ is zero
Over a cycle: net heat absorbed = net work done

segments.text: Now the subtle, exam-deciding distinction that separates a state from a flow.
Your bank balance is a state; at any instant it has one definite value. But income and expenditure describe flows during a period, not contents at an instant.
So internal energy U is a state function, while heat Q and work W are path functions. It is meaningless to ask how much heat is sitting in a gas right now.
Take a gas from state i to state f by ten wildly different routes. Heat and work differ on every single one.
Yet the change in internal energy is identical for all ten, because it depends only on the endpoints, never on the route between them.
So change in heat minus change in work comes out the same no matter the path. This path-independence of the internal-energy change is the single most-used idea in first-law problems.
A powerful corollary drops out. If the gas returns to its start, over that closed cycle the change in internal energy is zero.
So over a cycle, net heat absorbed equals net work done. That one line solves a huge fraction of cyclic-process questions.
अब वो subtle, exam-deciding फ़र्क़ जो एक state को एक flow से अलग करता है।
आपका bank balance एक state है; किसी भी instant पर उसकी एक definite value होती है। पर income और expenditure एक period के दौरान के flows बताते हैं, किसी instant का content नहीं।
तो internal energy U एक state function है, जबकि heat Q और work W path functions हैं। यह पूछना बेमानी है कि अभी gas में कितनी heat पड़ी है।
gas को state i से state f तक दस बिलकुल अलग रास्तों से ले जाओ। heat और work हर एक पर अलग होंगे।
फिर भी internal energy का change सभी दस के लिए identical होगा, क्योंकि यह सिर्फ़ endpoints पर depend करता है, बीच के रास्ते पर कभी नहीं।
तो change in heat minus change in work हर path पर एक ही निकलता है। internal-energy change की यह path-independence first-law problems का सबसे ज़्यादा use होने वाला idea है।
एक powerful corollary निकलता है। अगर gas अपनी शुरुआत पर लौट आए, उस closed cycle में internal energy का change शून्य होता है।
तो एक cycle में, net heat absorbed बराबर net work done. यह एक line cyclic-process सवालों का बड़ा हिस्सा हल कर देती है।

board_events.text: All three carry the dimension of energy

segments.text: Here is the compact toolkit: the master equation, the sign rules, and the four process shortcuts.

The master equation, in the board and exam convention: change in heat equals change in internal energy plus change in work. Equivalently, change in internal energy equals change in heat minus change in work.

The sign convention, memorise it exactly. Heat is positive when absorbed by the system. Work is positive when done by the gas, that is, on expansion. Internal energy positive means, for an ideal gas, the temperature rose.
Work done by a quasi-static gas is the integral of P with respect to V, which is simply the area under the P-V curve.
For an ideal gas the internal-energy change is n times C-V times the temperature change, and this holds for every process, not just constant volume.

An alternate-convention alert. Some chemistry texts write change in internal energy equals change in heat plus change in work, defining work as done on the system. Same physics, flipped sign. Pick one and never mix them mid-problem.
Each of the four standard processes is the master equation with exactly one term killed.
And a quick self-check: heat, work, and internal-energy change all share the dimension of energy. If they do not, the equation is not even dimensionally homogeneous.
यह रहा compact toolkit: master equation, sign rules, और चार process shortcuts.
master equation, board और exam convention में: change in heat बराबर change in internal energy plus change in work. यानी, change in internal energy बराबर change in heat minus change in work.
sign convention, इसे ठीक-ठीक याद रखो। heat positive है जब system absorb करे। work positive है जब gas करे, यानी expansion पर। internal energy positive यानी, ideal gas के लिए, temperature बढ़ी।
quasi-static gas का किया work है P का V के respect में integral, जो बस P-V curve के नीचे का area है।
ideal gas के लिए internal-energy change है n into C-V into temperature change, और यह हर process के लिए सही है, सिर्फ़ constant volume के लिए नहीं।

एक alternate-convention alert. कुछ chemistry texts लिखते हैं change in internal energy बराबर change in heat plus change in work, work को system पर किया हुआ मानते हुए। वही physics, उलटा sign. एक चुनो और problem के बीच कभी मत मिलाओ।
चारों standard processes में से हर एक master equation ही है, बस एक term मारा हुआ।
और एक quick self-check: heat, work, और internal-energy change सब energy का dimension रखते हैं। अगर नहीं, तो equation dimensionally homogeneous ही नहीं है।

Sanity check: compress with little heat out and $U$ must rise

segments.text: Two examples. The first tests unit care; the second is entirely about getting the signs right before you compute.
Board level. A gas is supplied two hundred fifty calories of heat, and as it heats it expands, doing five hundred joules of work on the surroundings. Find the internal-energy change.

First convert: two hundred fifty calories, at four point one eight joules each, is one thousand forty-five joules. Then the internal-energy change is that minus five hundred, giving positive five hundred forty-five joules.
The positive sign says internal energy increased by five hundred forty-five joules; most of the heat stayed inside the gas. Skipping the calorie-to-joule conversion would give nonsense.
Now the speed trap. A gas is compressed by an external agent doing eighty joules on it, and during compression it releases thirty joules of heat.
The whole trap is in the signs. Heat released means the heat change is negative thirty. Work done on the gas means the work done by the gas is negative eighty.
So the internal-energy change is negative thirty minus negative eighty, which is positive fifty joules. Internal energy rises.

A hurried student writes minus one hundred ten, forgetting that work on the gas is positive energy input. The sanity check rescues you: squeezing a gas while only a little heat leaks out must raise its internal energy.
दो examples. पहला unit care test करता है; दूसरा पूरी तरह इस बारे में है कि compute करने से पहले signs सही करो।
Board level. एक gas को two hundred fifty calories heat दी जाती है, और गरम होते हुए वो फैलती है, surroundings पर five hundred joules work करते हुए। internal-energy change निकालो।

पहले convert करो: two hundred fifty calories, हर एक four point one eight joules, यानी one thousand forty-five joules. फिर internal-energy change है वो minus five hundred, यानी positive five hundred forty-five joules.
positive sign कहता है internal energy five hundred forty-five joules बढ़ी; ज़्यादातर heat gas के अंदर ही रुक गई। calorie-to-joule conversion छोड़ना बकवास answer देगा।
अब speed trap. एक gas को external agent eighty joules करके compress करता है, और compression के दौरान वो thirty joules heat release करती है।
पूरा trap signs में है। heat released यानी heat change negative thirty. gas पर किया work यानी gas का किया work negative eighty.
तो internal-energy change है negative thirty minus negative eighty, यानी positive fifty joules. internal energy बढ़ती है।

एक जल्दबाज़ student minus one hundred ten लिखता है, यह भूलकर कि gas पर किया work positive energy input है। sanity check बचा लेता है: gas को दबाना जबकि थोड़ी ही heat निकले, internal energy बढ़ानी ही चाहिए।

State function: $\Delta U=+80$ J on path two too
Both fell, but the difference stayed pinned at $80$ J

segments.text: This problem lives entirely on internal energy being a state function. Learn the move once and reuse it everywhere.
A gas goes from A to B along two paths. Along path one it absorbs two hundred joules and does one hundred twenty joules of work. Along path two, same endpoints, it does sixty joules.
Find the heat exchanged along path two, and whether it is absorbed or released. Start from the fully known path.
From path one the internal-energy change from A to B is two hundred minus one hundred twenty, which is positive eighty joules.
Because internal energy is a state function, the change from A to B is the same eighty joules on path two, no matter how the gas travelled.
Now solve for the heat on path two: eighty plus the sixty joules of work, giving positive one hundred forty joules, absorbed by the gas.
Both transfers shrank from path one to path two, yet their difference stayed pinned at eighty joules. That fixed difference is the whole point.
यह problem पूरी तरह internal energy के state function होने पर टिका है। यह चाल एक बार सीखो और हर जगह दोहराओ।
एक gas A से B तक दो paths से जाती है। path one पर वो two hundred joules absorb करती है और one hundred twenty joules work करती है। path two पर, वही endpoints, वो sixty joules करती है।
path two पर exchange हुई heat निकालो, और यह कि वो absorb हुई या release. पूरी तरह पता path से शुरू करो।
path one से A से B तक internal-energy change है two hundred minus one hundred twenty, यानी positive eighty joules.
क्योंकि internal energy state function है, A से B तक change path two पर भी वही eighty joules है, चाहे gas कैसे भी गई हो।
अब path two पर heat के लिए solve करो: eighty plus sixty joules work, यानी positive one hundred forty joules, gas द्वारा absorb किया गया।
दोनों transfers path one से path two तक घटे, फिर भी उनका difference eighty joules पर टिका रहा। वही fixed difference पूरी बात है।

segments.text: An advanced example that layers the first law onto a phase change and reveals why latent heats are so large.
Two grams of liquid vaporise completely at constant pressure one point zero times ten to the fifth pascals. As liquid it fills two point five cubic centimetres; as vapour, thirty-one hundred.
The latent heat of vaporisation is two point zero times ten to the sixth joules per kilogram. First find the heat supplied.
The heat is the mass times the latent heat: two times ten to the minus three kilograms, times two times ten to the sixth, which is four thousand joules.
The work is isobaric. The volume change is thirty-one hundred minus two point five cubic centimetres, and pressure times that change is about three hundred ten joules.
So the internal-energy change is four thousand minus three hundred ten, about three thousand six hundred ninety joules, and its fraction of the heat is about ninety-two percent.
Only about eight percent pushed back the atmosphere; the ninety-two percent went into internal energy, almost all of it potential energy pulling molecules apart against their attractions.
This is exactly why latent heats are large. Breaking intermolecular bonds is expensive, while mechanical expansion is cheap, and the temperature holds constant while it boils.
एक advanced example जो first law को phase change पर चढ़ाता है और बताता है कि latent heats इतनी बड़ी क्यों होती हैं।
दो grams liquid पूरी तरह constant pressure one point zero into ten to the fifth pascals पर vaporise होता है। liquid में यह two point five cubic centimetres भरता है; vapour में, thirty-one hundred.
vaporisation की latent heat है two point zero into ten to the sixth joules per kilogram. पहले supply हुई heat निकालो।
heat है mass into latent heat: two into ten to the minus three kilograms, into two into ten to the sixth, यानी four thousand joules.
work isobaric है। volume change है thirty-one hundred minus two point five cubic centimetres, और pressure into वो change लगभग three hundred ten joules है।
तो internal-energy change है four thousand minus three hundred ten, लगभग three thousand six hundred ninety joules, और heat का इसका हिस्सा लगभग ninety-two percent है।
सिर्फ़ लगभग eight percent atmosphere को पीछे धकेलने में गया; वो ninety-two percent internal energy में गया, लगभग सारा का सारा potential energy molecules को उनकी attractions के खिलाफ़ अलग करते हुए।
यही वजह है कि latent heats बड़ी होती हैं। intermolecular bonds तोड़ना महँगा है, जबकि mechanical expansion सस्ता, और उबलते वक़्त temperature constant रहती है।

sections.title: Common pitfalls and pro-tips

board_events.text: Four traps, two speed habits
1. Signs before sums: decide every sign first
2. A gas has internal energy, not heat content
3. One unit for all three: $1$ cal $=4.18$ J
4. $\Delta U=0$ only for isothermal ideal gas or a full cycle
Two-path: compute $\Delta U$ once, then reuse
Cyclic: net heat = net work = enclosed area

segments.text: Master the sign convention and you have already won half of this chapter. Here are the four traps and two speed habits.

Trap one, the number-one error. Sign-convention chaos. Heat released makes the heat change negative; work done on the gas makes the work change negative. Decide and write every sign before you substitute.
Trap two. Calling internal energy heat content. A gas in a state has internal energy; it does not contain heat. Heat is energy crossing the boundary, defined only for a process.
Trap three. Forgetting unit consistency. Heat, internal energy, and work must share one unit. Convert first: one calorie is four point one eight joules.
Trap four. Assuming the internal-energy change is zero when it is not. It is zero only for an isothermal ideal gas or a complete cycle, never for adiabatic, isobaric, or isochoric.
Speed habit one. For any two-path problem, do not grind through both. Compute the internal-energy change once from the fully specified path, then reuse it.
Speed habit two. For cyclic problems jump straight to net heat equals net work, reading net work as the enclosed loop area, and always run the physical check that a compressed gas warms.
sign convention पर पकड़ बना लो और आप इस chapter का आधा जीत चुके। यह रहे चार traps और दो speed habits.
Trap एक, number-one error. Sign-convention chaos. heat released heat change को negative करता है; gas पर किया work, work change को negative. हर sign तय करके substitute से पहले लिखो।
Trap दो। internal energy को heat content कहना। किसी state की gas internal energy रखती है; वो heat contain नहीं करती। heat boundary पार करती energy है, सिर्फ़ एक process के लिए defined.
Trap तीन। unit consistency भूलना। heat, internal energy, और work एक unit share करें। पहले convert करो: one calorie है four point one eight joules.
Trap चार। internal-energy change को शून्य मान लेना जब वो नहीं है। यह सिर्फ़ isothermal ideal gas या पूरे cycle के लिए शून्य है, adiabatic, isobaric, या isochoric के लिए कभी नहीं।
Speed habit एक। किसी भी two-path problem में, दोनों को मत घिसो। internal-energy change एक बार पूरी तरह पता path से निकालो, फिर उसे reuse करो।
Speed habit दो। cyclic problems में सीधे net heat बराबर net work पर जाओ, net work को enclosed loop area पढ़ते हुए, और हमेशा physical check चलाओ कि compressed gas गरम होती है।

board_events.text: Isochoric ($V$ fixed): zero work, all heat into $U$
Isobaric ($P$ fixed): expands against steady pressure
Isothermal ($T$ fixed): $U$ constant, done slowly
Adiabatic (no heat): pays from $U$, so it cools
Isothermal and adiabatic: the slow and fast extremes
Adiabatic always falls more steeply than isothermal

segments.text: <curious>We have the universal accountant, change in heat equals change in internal energy plus work. But an accountant needs the rules of the particular transaction to fill in the numbers.
Pin down the rule and the first law instantly tells you how heat, work, and internal energy divide up. Imagine four ways to handle the same cylinder, each holding one thing fixed.
On a P-V diagram all four start from a common point and go their own way.

Volume fixed, isochoric. Bolt the piston so it cannot move; heat the gas and pressure climbs, but the gas does zero work. Every joule goes into internal energy, like a sealed pressure cooker with a jammed lid.
Pressure fixed, isobaric. Let the piston slide freely against the atmosphere; heat the gas and it expands, doing work while warming, like water boiling in an open pan.

Temperature fixed, isothermal. Keep the cylinder in a giant bath and move the piston slowly, so heat sneaks in to replace every joule spent as work. Internal energy never changes. Slow is the key word.

No heat exchanged, adiabatic. Wrap it in insulation, or move the piston so fast heat cannot flow. Now the gas pays for expansion out of its own internal energy, so it cools, like a spray can hissing cold.

Isothermal and adiabatic are two opposite extremes of speed: infinitely slow with the bath connected, or so fast that no heat crosses. Real processes live in between; exams idealise to these clean limits.
On a P-V diagram both fall as curves, but the adiabatic always falls more steeply, because the sealed gas loses temperature as it expands and so loses pressure faster.
<curious>हमारे पास universal accountant है, change in heat बराबर change in internal energy plus work. पर accountant को numbers भरने के लिए उस ख़ास transaction के rules चाहिए।
rule तय करो और first law तुरंत बता देता है कि heat, work, और internal energy कैसे बँटेंगे। सोचो, एक ही cylinder को handle करने के चार तरीक़े, हर एक एक चीज़ fixed रखता है।
एक P-V diagram पर चारों एक common point से शुरू होकर अपनी-अपनी राह जाते हैं।

Volume fixed, isochoric. piston को bolt कर दो ताकि हिले नहीं; gas गरम करो और pressure चढ़ती है, पर gas zero work करती है। हर joule internal energy में जाता है, जैसे jammed ढक्कन वाला sealed pressure cooker.
Pressure fixed, isobaric. piston को atmosphere के against freely सरकने दो; gas गरम करो और वो फैलती है, गरम होते हुए work करते हुए, जैसे खुले pan में उबलता पानी.
Temperature fixed, isothermal. cylinder को एक बड़े bath में रखो और piston धीरे सरकाओ, ताकि heat अंदर आकर work में खर्च हुआ हर joule replace कर दे। internal energy कभी नहीं बदलती। Slow key word है.

No heat exchanged, adiabatic. इसे insulation में लपेटो, या piston इतना तेज़ चलाओ कि heat बह न सके। अब gas expansion की क़ीमत अपनी internal energy से चुकाती है, तो ठंडी होती है, जैसे spray can ठंडी फुफकारती हुई.
Isothermal और adiabatic speed के दो opposite extremes हैं: bath से जुड़े हुए बेहद धीमा, या इतना तेज़ कि कोई heat पार न करे। असली processes बीच में रहती हैं; exams इन साफ़ limits पर idealise करते हैं।
P-V diagram पर दोनों curves की तरह गिरती हैं, पर adiabatic हमेशा ज़्यादा तेज़ी से गिरती है, क्योंकि sealed gas फैलते वक़्त temperature खोती है और इसलिए pressure तेज़ी से।

board_events.text: Different paths, different areas: $W$ is path-dependent
Cycle work = the area enclosed by the loop
Enclosed area is the engine’s output per cycle
Needs quasi-static: one defined pressure at each instant
Free expansion into vacuum: expands, yet zero work
Ideal-gas relations; real gases deviate at extremes

segments.text: Here is the deepest single fact in this subtopic, and the one geometric idea behind every heat-engine problem.
The work done by a gas equals the area under its P-V curve, the accumulated pressure times each small volume change.
Two processes connecting the same two states enclose different areas, and so do different work. That is a direct picture of why work is a path function.
And if the process traces a closed loop, a cycle, the work done per cycle is exactly the area trapped inside the loop.
That single idea, enclosed area equals work per cycle, drives every heat-engine problem you will ever meet.
One condition. The clean formula, work equals the integral of P over volume, needs a quasi-static process, slow enough that the gas has one well-defined pressure at every instant.
The classic exception is free expansion. A gas rushing into a vacuum does zero work despite expanding, because there is nothing pushing back and no single pressure.
And the process relations we build next are derived for an ideal gas; real gases deviate at high pressure or low temperature.
यह रहा इस subtopic का सबसे गहरा एक fact, और हर heat-engine problem के पीछे का एक geometric idea.
gas का किया work उसके P-V curve के नीचे के area के बराबर है, जमा हुआ pressure into हर छोटा volume change.
एक ही दो states को जोड़ती दो processes अलग-अलग area घेरती हैं, और इसलिए अलग work करती हैं। यही सीधा चित्र है कि work path function क्यों है।
और अगर process एक closed loop बनाए, एक cycle, तो हर cycle का work ठीक loop के अंदर फँसा area है।
वो एक idea, enclosed area बराबर work per cycle, हर heat-engine problem को चलाता है जो आपको कभी मिलेगा।
एक condition. साफ़ formula, work बराबर P का volume पर integral, को quasi-static process चाहिए, इतना धीमा कि gas का हर instant पर एक well-defined pressure हो।
classic exception है free expansion. vacuum में दौड़ती gas फैलने के बावजूद zero work करती है, क्योंकि पीछे धकेलने वाला कुछ नहीं और कोई single pressure नहीं।
और आगे जो process relations हम बनाएँगे, वे ideal gas के लिए derive हैं; असली gases high pressure या low temperature पर deviate करती हैं।

board_events.text: Adiabatic is $\gamma\times$ steeper; $\gamma=\tfrac{5}{3},\tfrac{7}{5},\tfrac{4}{3}$

segments.text: The complete formula sheet: four processes, the adiabatic relations, and the single polytropic law that contains them all.
Isochoric, volume constant: the work is zero, so the heat equals the internal-energy change, which is n times C-V times the temperature change.
Isobaric, pressure constant: the work is pressure times the volume change, equal to n R times the temperature change, and the heat is n times C-P times the temperature change.
Isothermal, temperature constant: the internal-energy change is zero, so the heat equals the work, which is n R T times the natural log of final over initial volume.
Adiabatic, no heat: the internal-energy change is minus the work, and the work is initial P V minus final P V, all over gamma minus one, equal to n R times the temperature drop over gamma minus one.
The adiabatic relations come in three equivalent forms: P V to the gamma is constant, T V to the gamma minus one is constant, and P to the one minus gamma times T to the gamma is constant.

The polytropic law is the master: P V to the x is constant, with work n R times the temperature change over one minus x, and molar heat capacity C-V plus R over one minus x. Setting x to zero, one, gamma, or infinity recovers all four processes.
The slope of a polytropic curve is minus x times pressure over volume, so at a common point the isobaric slope is zero, the isothermal is minus P over V, and the adiabatic is minus gamma P over V.
So the adiabatic curve is gamma times steeper than the isothermal. Remember gamma: five thirds for monoatomic, seven fifths for diatomic, four thirds for polyatomic.
पूरी formula sheet: चार processes, adiabatic relations, और वो एक polytropic law जो इन सबको समेटता है।
Isochoric, volume constant: work zero है, तो heat बराबर internal-energy change, जो है n into C-V into temperature change.
Isobaric, pressure constant: work है pressure into volume change, बराबर n R into temperature change, और heat है n into C-P into temperature change.
Isothermal, temperature constant: internal-energy change zero है, तो heat बराबर work, जो है n R T into natural log of final over initial volume.
Adiabatic, no heat: internal-energy change है minus work, और work है initial P V minus final P V, बटा gamma minus one, बराबर n R into temperature drop over gamma minus one.
adiabatic relations तीन equivalent forms में आती हैं: P V to the gamma constant, T V to the gamma minus one constant, और P to the one minus gamma into T to the gamma constant.

polytropic law master है: P V to the x constant, work n R into temperature change over one minus x, और molar heat capacity C-V plus R over one minus x. x को zero, one, gamma, या infinity रखने पर चारों processes वापस मिल जाती हैं।
polytropic curve का slope है minus x into pressure over volume, तो एक common point पर isobaric slope zero, isothermal minus P over V, और adiabatic minus gamma P over V.
तो adiabatic curve isothermal से gamma गुना steeper है। gamma याद रखो: monoatomic के लिए five thirds, diatomic के लिए seven fifths, polyatomic के लिए four thirds.

board_events.text: $\Delta U=0$, so all the work is supplied as heat

segments.text: The first board favourite. Master the reasoning, not just the algebra, because examiners want the logic.
Setup. Let n moles of an ideal gas expand quasi-statically and isothermally, the temperature held at T, from initial volume to final volume.
The work will be the shaded area under this isotherm, the integral of pressure across the volume change.
Step one, pressure in terms of volume. From the gas law, P equals n R T over V.
Step two, the work integral. Work is the integral of P over volume, which is the integral of n R T over V, with respect to V.
Step three, integrate. Pull out the constants n, R, and T, and the integral of one over V is the natural log, giving n R T times the log of final over initial volume.

Step four, an alternate form. Since temperature is constant, initial P V equals final P V, so the volume ratio equals the reversed pressure ratio, giving n R T times the log of initial over final pressure.
The physical reading. With the internal-energy change zero, the first law forces the heat to equal the work. Every joule the gas spends is supplied as heat by the reservoir.
पहला board favourite. सिर्फ़ algebra नहीं, reasoning पर पकड़ बनाओ, क्योंकि examiners logic चाहते हैं।
Setup. मान लो n moles ideal gas quasi-statically और isothermally फैलती है, temperature T पर रखी, initial volume से final volume तक।
work इस isotherm के नीचे का shaded area होगा, pressure का volume change पर integral.
Step one, pressure को volume के terms में। gas law से, P बराबर n R T over V.
Step two, work integral. work है P का volume पर integral, यानी n R T over V का integral, V के respect में।
Step three, integrate. constants n, R, और T बाहर निकालो, और one over V का integral natural log है, यानी n R T into log of final over initial volume.
Step four, एक alternate form. temperature constant है, तो initial P V बराबर final P V, यानी volume ratio उलटे pressure ratio के बराबर, देते हुए n R T into log of initial over final pressure.
physical reading. internal-energy change zero होने से, first law heat को work के बराबर कर देता है। gas जो भी joule खर्च करती है, वो reservoir से heat के रूप में आता है।

segments.text: The second board favourite, and the more demanding one. We derive P V to the gamma is constant from the first law itself.
Setup. A quasi-static adiabatic process, so the heat exchanged is zero at every step.
Step one, the first law on an infinitesimal step. With heat zero, the internal-energy change n C-V d T plus P d V must sum to zero.
Step two, eliminate the temperature change. Differentiate the gas law: P d V plus V d P equals n R d T. Substitute, multiply through by n R, and collect terms.
Step three, introduce gamma. Using Mayer's relation, C-P equals C-V plus R, this becomes C-V V d P plus C-P P d V equals zero. Divide by C-V P V and use gamma equals C-P over C-V.

Step four, integrate. The log of P plus gamma times the log of V is constant, which means P V to the gamma is constant. Substituting back gives T V to the gamma minus one, and P to the one minus gamma times T to the gamma.
Step five, the work. Compare the same expansion done isothermally and adiabatically: the isothermal encloses the larger area.

Integrating P equals K over V to the gamma gives the work as initial P V minus final P V over gamma minus one. With heat zero, this work equals minus the internal-energy change, so an adiabatic expansion cools the gas, the spray-can effect.
दूसरा board favourite, और ज़्यादा मुश्किल। हम P V to the gamma constant को first law से ही derive करते हैं।
Setup. एक quasi-static adiabatic process, तो हर step पर exchange हुई heat zero है।
Step one, एक infinitesimal step पर first law। heat zero होने पर, internal-energy change n C-V d T plus P d V का योग zero होना चाहिए।
Step two, temperature change हटाओ। gas law को differentiate करो: P d V plus V d P बराबर n R d T. substitute करो, n R से गुणा करो, और terms इकट्ठा करो।
Step three, gamma लाओ। Mayer's relation से, C-P बराबर C-V plus R, यह बनता है C-V V d P plus C-P P d V बराबर zero. C-V P V से भाग दो और gamma बराबर C-P over C-V use करो।
Step four, integrate. log of P plus gamma into log of V constant, यानी P V to the gamma constant. वापस substitute करने पर T V to the gamma minus one, और P to the one minus gamma into T to the gamma.
Step five, work. एक ही expansion isothermally और adiabatically करके compare करो: isothermal बड़ा area घेरती है।

P बराबर K over V to the gamma को integrate करने पर work मिलता है initial P V minus final P V over gamma minus one. heat zero होने से, यह work बराबर minus internal-energy change, तो adiabatic expansion gas को ठंडा करती है, spray-can effect.

board_events.text: Heat in equals work out; $T$ and $U$ unchanged
Monoatomic, $\gamma=\tfrac{5}{3}$, compressed to $V/8$
Temperature quadruples: $T_f=4T_i$
Compression raises $T$, so the factor exceeds one

segments.text: Two applications: one uses the isothermal work we just derived, the other is a quick adiabatic ratio trap.
Board level. Two point zero moles at three hundred kelvin expand isothermally until the volume triples.

The isothermal work is n R T times the natural log of three: two times eight point three one four times three hundred times one point zero nine nine, about five point four eight kilojoules. Since the internal-energy change is zero, the heat absorbed equals that.
All the absorbed heat leaves as work; temperature and internal energy are unchanged. That is the signature of an isothermal step.
Speed trap. A monoatomic gas, gamma five thirds, is compressed adiabatically until its volume becomes one-eighth. By what factor does its absolute temperature change?

Use T V to the gamma minus one is constant. The ratio of final to initial temperature is eight to the two-thirds. Since eight is two cubed, this is two to the power three times two-thirds, which is two squared, equal to four.
So the temperature quadruples. The classic mistakes are using gamma instead of gamma minus one, or inverting the volume ratio.
The physical check saves you: compression must raise temperature, so the factor has to exceed one. That instantly kills the wrong answer of one-quarter.
दो applications: एक अभी derive किया isothermal work use करता है, दूसरा एक quick adiabatic ratio trap है।
Board level. two point zero moles three hundred kelvin पर isothermally फैलती हैं जब तक volume तिगुना न हो।

isothermal work है n R T into natural log of three: two into eight point three one four into three hundred into one point zero nine nine, लगभग five point four eight kilojoules. internal-energy change zero होने से, absorb हुई heat उतनी ही।
सारी absorb हुई heat work बनकर निकल जाती है; temperature और internal energy अनबदली रहती हैं। यही isothermal step की पहचान है।
Speed trap. एक monoatomic gas, gamma five thirds, adiabatically compress होती है जब तक volume एक-आठवाँ न हो। इसकी absolute temperature किस factor से बदलती है?

T V to the gamma minus one constant use करो। final से initial temperature का ratio है eight to the two-thirds. eight दो cubed है, तो यह two to the power three into two-thirds, यानी two squared, बराबर four.
तो temperature चौगुनी हो जाती है। classic mistakes हैं gamma minus one की जगह gamma use करना, या volume ratio उलट देना।
physical check बचा लेता है: compression को temperature बढ़ानी ही है, तो factor एक से ज़्यादा होना चाहिए। यह तुरंत one-quarter वाला ग़लत answer मार देता है।

board_events.text: Heat splits as $C_P:C_V=7:5$ for a diatomic gas

segments.text: A clean isobaric numerical for a diatomic gas, where all three energies split in a fixed ratio.
Three point zero moles of a diatomic ideal gas, gamma seven fifths, so C-V is five halves R and C-P is seven halves R, are heated at constant pressure so the temperature rises by one hundred kelvin.
The isobaric work is n R times the temperature change: three times eight point three one four times one hundred, about two point four nine kilojoules.
The internal-energy change is n times C-V times the temperature change: three times five halves of eight point three one four, times one hundred, about six point two four kilojoules.
The heat supplied is n times C-P times the temperature change: three times seven halves of eight point three one four, times one hundred, about eight point seven three kilojoules.
Watch how the heat divides into internal energy and work.
Verify the first law: the internal-energy change plus the work is six point two four plus two point four nine, which is eight point seven three kilojoules, exactly the heat. It checks out.
The heat splits in the ratio C-P to C-V, which is seven to five for a diatomic gas. That ratio is a quick structural check for any isobaric problem.
एक diatomic gas के लिए साफ़ isobaric numerical, जहाँ तीनों energies एक fixed ratio में बँटती हैं।
three point zero moles diatomic ideal gas, gamma seven fifths, तो C-V है five halves R और C-P है seven halves R, constant pressure पर गरम की जाती हैं ताकि temperature one hundred kelvin बढ़े।
isobaric work है n R into temperature change: three into eight point three one four into one hundred, लगभग two point four nine kilojoules.
internal-energy change है n into C-V into temperature change: three into five halves of eight point three one four, into one hundred, लगभग six point two four kilojoules.
supply हुई heat है n into C-P into temperature change: three into seven halves of eight point three one four, into one hundred, लगभग eight point seven three kilojoules.
देखो heat कैसे internal energy और work में बँटती है।
first law verify करो: internal-energy change plus work है six point two four plus two point four nine, यानी eight point seven three kilojoules, ठीक heat जितना। सही बैठता है।
heat, C-P to C-V के ratio में बँटती है, जो diatomic gas के लिए seven to five है। वो ratio किसी भी isobaric problem का quick structural check है।

board_events.text: Isothermal does about $25\%$ more work
Expansion work: isobaric $\gt$ isothermal $\gt$ adiabatic

segments.text: An advanced comparison that captures the geometric truth behind expansion-work ordering.
A monoatomic gas, gamma five thirds, starts at P-naught and V-naught and expands to twice V-naught by two routes, isothermal and adiabatic.
The isothermal work, with n R T equal to P-naught V-naught, is P-naught V-naught times the natural log of two, about zero point six nine three P-naught V-naught.
For the adiabatic, the final pressure is P-naught times two to the minus gamma, so the final P V is P-naught V-naught times two to the minus two-thirds.

The adiabatic work is initial minus final P V over gamma minus one, which is three halves P-naught V-naught times one minus two to the minus two-thirds, about zero point five five five P-naught V-naught.
So the ratio of isothermal to adiabatic work is zero point six nine three over zero point five five five, about one point two five.
So the isothermal expansion does about twenty-five percent more work. Both start together and end at the same volume, yet the fed isotherm keeps its temperature, and its pressure, higher throughout.
Higher pressure throughout means a larger area under the curve, hence more work. This is the geometric truth behind the rule: isobaric, then isothermal, then adiabatic, in decreasing expansion work.
एक advanced comparison जो expansion-work ordering के पीछे का geometric सच पकड़ती है।
एक monoatomic gas, gamma five thirds, P-naught और V-naught से शुरू होकर दो routes से twice V-naught तक फैलती है, isothermal और adiabatic.
isothermal work, n R T बराबर P-naught V-naught के साथ, है P-naught V-naught into natural log of two, लगभग zero point six nine three P-naught V-naught.
adiabatic के लिए, final pressure है P-naught into two to the minus gamma, तो final P V है P-naught V-naught into two to the minus two-thirds.
adiabatic work है initial minus final P V over gamma minus one, यानी three halves P-naught V-naught into one minus two to the minus two-thirds, लगभग zero point five five five P-naught V-naught.
तो isothermal से adiabatic work का ratio है zero point six nine three over zero point five five five, लगभग one point two five.
तो isothermal expansion लगभग twenty-five percent ज़्यादा work करती है। दोनों साथ शुरू होकर एक ही volume पर ख़त्म होती हैं, फिर भी fed isotherm अपनी temperature, और pressure, पूरे रास्ते ऊँची रखती है।
पूरे रास्ते ऊँचा pressure यानी curve के नीचे बड़ा area, इसलिए ज़्यादा work। यही geometric सच है उस rule के पीछे: isobaric, फिर isothermal, फिर adiabatic, घटते expansion work में।

sections.title: Common pitfalls and pro-tips

board_events.text: Four traps, then the speed habits
1. Adiabatic is steeper and changes temperature
2. Pressure uses $\gamma$; temperature uses $\gamma-1$
3. Each work formula belongs to one process only
4. Cycle work = enclosed area; clockwise is an engine
Adiabatic: work in ratios, not absolute pressures
Read a graph: vertical, horizontal, or the steeper curve

segments.text: Master the four processes and the polytropic generalisation, and the rest of thermodynamics is just assembly. Here are the traps.

Trap one. Confusing the isothermal and adiabatic curves. They look like twins, but the adiabatic is steeper, the adiabatic gas changes temperature while the isothermal does not, and heat equals work is isothermal while internal energy equals minus work is adiabatic.
Trap two. Using gamma where gamma minus one belongs. The pressure relation uses gamma, in P V to the gamma; the temperature relation uses gamma minus one, in T V to the gamma minus one.
Trap three. Applying a process formula outside its process. The n R T log formula is only isothermal; pressure times volume change is only isobaric.

Trap four. Sign and direction of work. Expansion is positive, compression negative. For a cycle, net work is the enclosed area, positive if the loop runs clockwise, an engine, and negative if anticlockwise, a refrigerator.
Speed habit. For adiabatic numericals work with ratios, never absolute pressures. Final over initial temperature is the volume ratio to the gamma minus one, and the pressure ratio uses gamma.
And to identify a process from a graph in seconds: a vertical line is isochoric, a horizontal line is isobaric, and of the two curves the steeper one is always adiabatic.
चार processes और polytropic generalisation पर पकड़ बना लो, और बाक़ी thermodynamics बस assembly है। यह रहे traps.

Trap एक। isothermal और adiabatic curves को confuse करना। वे जुड़वाँ दिखती हैं, पर adiabatic steeper है, adiabatic gas temperature बदलती है जबकि isothermal नहीं, और heat बराबर work isothermal है जबकि internal energy बराबर minus work adiabatic.
Trap दो। gamma minus one की जगह gamma use करना। pressure relation gamma use करती है, P V to the gamma में; temperature relation gamma minus one, T V to the gamma minus one में।
Trap तीन। किसी process formula को उसके process के बाहर लगाना। n R T log formula सिर्फ़ isothermal है; pressure into volume change सिर्फ़ isobaric.

Trap चार। work का sign और direction. expansion positive, compression negative. cycle के लिए, net work enclosed area है, clockwise loop पर positive, एक engine, और anticlockwise पर negative, एक refrigerator.
Speed habit. adiabatic numericals में ratios से काम करो, कभी absolute pressures से नहीं। final over initial temperature है volume ratio to the gamma minus one, और pressure ratio gamma use करता है।
और किसी graph से process seconds में पहचानने को: vertical line isochoric है, horizontal line isobaric, और दो curves में steeper वाली हमेशा adiabatic.

board_events.text: Constant volume: all heat into $U$, capacity $C_V$
Constant pressure: some heat does work, capacity $C_P$
A gas has two: $C_V$ and $C_P$, with $C_P\gt C_V$ always
Leaky bucket: the leak is the work of expansion

segments.text: <curious>Pour the same heat into a small steel spanner and into a bucket of water. The spanner's temperature shoots up while the water barely warms. That reluctance is heat capacity.
Divide by mass and you get the specific heat capacity, per kilogram. Divide by moles and you get the molar specific heat. Water's famously large value is why coastal cities stay mild.
For solids and liquids one number is enough; they barely expand, so nearly all the heat becomes internal energy. Gases are different, and this is the heart of the subtopic.
Heat a gas in a sealed rigid box and it cannot expand; heat it under a free piston and it does. The same gas then needs two molar heats.
Heat it at constant volume and every joule goes into internal energy, because the piston cannot move. That defines the molar heat at constant volume, C-V.
Heat it at constant pressure and the gas expands, spending some of the incoming heat pushing the piston back. So you must supply extra heat for the same temperature rise; that is C-P.
So a gas needs two molar specific heats, C-V at constant volume and C-P at constant pressure, and it is always true that C-P is greater than C-V.
Picture a leaky bucket. Plug the leak and every mug raises the level; that is C-V. Leave the leak open and some drains away, so you pour more; that is C-P. The leak is exactly the expansion work.
<curious>एक छोटे steel spanner और एक बाल्टी पानी में same heat डालो। spanner का temperature उछल जाता है जबकि पानी मुश्किल से गरम होता है। वही reluctance है heat capacity.
mass से भाग दो तो मिलता है specific heat capacity, per kilogram. moles से भाग दो तो molar specific heat. पानी का मशहूर बड़ा value ही वजह है कि coastal cities हल्के मौसम की रहती हैं।
solids और liquids के लिए एक number काफ़ी है; वे मुश्किल से फैलते हैं, तो लगभग सारी heat internal energy बन जाती है। Gases अलग हैं, और यही इस subtopic का दिल है।
gas को sealed rigid box में गरम करो और वो फैल नहीं सकती; free piston के नीचे गरम करो और वो फैलती है। वही gas तब दो molar heats माँगती है।
constant volume पर गरम करो और हर joule internal energy में जाता है, क्योंकि piston हिल नहीं सकता। यही define करता है constant volume पर molar heat, C-V.
constant pressure पर गरम करो और gas फैलती है, आती हुई heat का कुछ हिस्सा piston को पीछे धकेलने में खर्च करते हुए। तो same temperature rise के लिए आपको extra heat देनी होगी; वही है C-P.
तो gas को दो molar specific heats चाहिए, constant volume पर C-V और constant pressure पर C-P, और यह हमेशा सच है कि C-P, C-V से बड़ा है।
एक leaky बाल्टी सोचो। leak बंद करो और हर मग level बढ़ाता है; वही C-V. leak खुली छोड़ो और कुछ बह जाता है, तो ज़्यादा डालना पड़ता है; वही C-P. वो leak ठीक expansion work है।

board_events.text: Monoatomic: three translational degrees of freedom
Diatomic: three translations plus two rotations, five in all
Equipartition: each degree gets $\tfrac{1}{2}k_BT$ per molecule
More wiggles, more storage: bigger $C_V$, smaller $\gamma$
Room temperature: vibration frozen, so $f=5$, not $7$

segments.text: Why is C-V three halves R for helium but five halves R for nitrogen? Because internal energy is stored in the ways a molecule can move.
A point-like monoatomic atom can only translate in three directions; a dumbbell-shaped diatomic molecule can also tumble about two axes.
So a monoatomic atom has three degrees of freedom, all translational. Helium, argon, and the like store energy in just those three.
A diatomic molecule adds two rotational degrees at room temperature, making five. That is why nitrogen and oxygen store more energy than a single atom.
The equipartition theorem hands each active degree of freedom an energy of one half k B T per molecule, that is one half R per mole per kelvin.
So a molecule with f active degrees stores internal energy f over two n R T, which gives C-V equal to f over two, times R.
More ways to wiggle means more places to hide energy, which means a larger heat capacity, and a smaller gamma.
One guardrail. For diatomic gases at room temperature, rotation is active but vibration is usually frozen, so f is five, not seven. Use seven only when a problem invokes high-temperature vibration.
helium के लिए C-V three halves R क्यों पर nitrogen के लिए five halves R? क्योंकि internal energy molecule के हिलने के तरीक़ों में stored होती है।
एक point जैसा monoatomic atom सिर्फ़ तीन directions में translate कर सकता है; एक dumbbell जैसा diatomic molecule दो axes के बारे में tumble भी कर सकता है।
तो monoatomic atom के तीन degrees of freedom हैं, सब translational. helium, argon, और ऐसी gases सिर्फ़ उन तीन में energy रखती हैं।
एक diatomic molecule room temperature पर दो rotational degrees जोड़ता है, कुल पाँच। इसीलिए nitrogen और oxygen एक atom से ज़्यादा energy रखते हैं।
equipartition theorem हर active degree of freedom को one half k B T per molecule energy देता है, यानी one half R per mole per kelvin.
तो f active degrees वाला molecule internal energy f over two n R T रखता है, जो देता है C-V बराबर f over two, into R.
जितने ज़्यादा wiggle करने के तरीक़े, उतनी ज़्यादा जगह energy छिपाने की, यानी बड़ा heat capacity, और छोटा gamma.

एक guardrail. diatomic gases के लिए room temperature पर rotation active है पर vibration आमतौर पर frozen, तो f पाँच है, सात नहीं। सात सिर्फ़ तब use करो जब problem high-temperature vibration की बात करे।

segments.text: The compact sheet: definitions, Mayer, equipartition, the reflex identities, and mixtures.
Heat by specific capacity is mass times s times the temperature change; by molar capacity it is n times C times the temperature change.
Mayer's relation, per mole for an ideal gas: C-P minus C-V equals R. The difference is exactly the expansion work.
From equipartition: C-V is f over two R, C-P is f over two plus one, times R, and gamma is one plus two over f.
Here are the standard values you should keep in reflex memory.

Two reflex identities convert any gamma straight into capacities: C-V is R over gamma minus one, and C-P is gamma R over gamma minus one. And the internal-energy change is n C-V times the temperature change, in every process.
For a polytropic process the molar heat capacity is C-V plus R over one minus x, recovering C-P at x zero, infinity at x one, zero at x gamma, and C-V as x grows without bound.

Useful benchmarks: water's specific heat is about four thousand one hundred eighty-six joules per kilogram per kelvin. For a mixture, mole-weight each capacity, then apply Mayer, then take the ratio for gamma.
compact sheet: definitions, Mayer, equipartition, reflex identities, और mixtures.
specific capacity से heat है mass into s into temperature change; molar capacity से यह n into C into temperature change.
Mayer's relation, ideal gas के लिए per mole: C-P minus C-V बराबर R. यह difference ठीक expansion work है।
equipartition से: C-V है f over two R, C-P है f over two plus one, into R, और gamma है one plus two over f.
यह रहे standard values जो reflex memory में रखने चाहिए।

दो reflex identities किसी भी gamma को सीधे capacities में बदल देती हैं: C-V है R over gamma minus one, और C-P है gamma R over gamma minus one. और internal-energy change है n C-V into temperature change, हर process में।
polytropic process के लिए molar heat capacity है C-V plus R over one minus x, जो x zero पर C-P, x one पर infinity, x gamma पर zero, और x बहुत बड़ा होने पर C-V देती है।

काम के benchmarks: पानी का specific heat लगभग four thousand one hundred eighty-six joules per kilogram per kelvin है। mixture के लिए, हर capacity को mole-weight करो, फिर Mayer लगाओ, फिर gamma के लिए ratio लो।

board_events.text: The extra $R$ is the expansion work per mole per kelvin

segments.text: A board favourite. We heat one mole by the same tiny amount, once at constant volume and once at constant pressure, and compare.
Setup. Take one mole of an ideal gas. Heat it by a small temperature change, first holding volume fixed, then holding pressure fixed.
At constant volume no work is done, so the heat equals the internal-energy change, C-V d T. For an ideal gas this dU equals C-V d T holds for every process, not just this one.
At constant pressure the heat is the internal-energy change plus the work: C-V d T plus P d V, and by definition this equals C-P d T.
The two heatings reach the same temperature rise, but the constant-pressure one needs an extra piece.
Evaluate that extra piece from the gas law. For one mole at constant pressure, differentiating P V equals R T gives P d V equals R d T.
Substitute. C-P d T equals C-V d T plus R d T, and cancelling d T gives C-P minus C-V equals R.
The extra R is precisely the work P d V done pushing back the surroundings, per mole per kelvin. That leak is why C-P exceeds C-V always, and by exactly R.
एक board favourite. हम one mole को same tiny amount से गरम करते हैं, एक बार constant volume पर और एक बार constant pressure पर, और compare करते हैं।
Setup. one mole ideal gas लो। इसे एक छोटे temperature change से गरम करो, पहले volume fixed रखते हुए, फिर pressure fixed रखते हुए।
constant volume पर कोई work नहीं होता, तो heat बराबर internal-energy change, C-V d T. ideal gas के लिए यह dU बराबर C-V d T हर process के लिए सही है, सिर्फ़ इसके लिए नहीं।
constant pressure पर heat है internal-energy change plus work: C-V d T plus P d V, और definition से यह बराबर C-P d T.
दोनों heatings same temperature rise तक पहुँचती हैं, पर constant-pressure वाली को एक extra piece चाहिए।
उस extra piece को gas law से निकालो। one mole के लिए constant pressure पर, P V बराबर R T को differentiate करने पर P d V बराबर R d T.
substitute करो। C-P d T बराबर C-V d T plus R d T, और d T cancel करने पर C-P minus C-V बराबर R.
वो extra R ठीक वो work P d V है जो surroundings को पीछे धकेलने में लगता है, per mole per kelvin. वही leak वजह है कि C-P हमेशा C-V से ज़्यादा है, और ठीक R जितना।

board_events.text: Work fraction $=R/C_P=2/(f+2)$
Monoatomic wins: $2/5=40\%$

segments.text: One clean identification, and one NEET-style trap about which gas does the most expansion work.
Board level. A gas has constant-volume molar heat twenty point eight joules per mole per kelvin. Identify the gas, and find its constant-pressure heat and its gamma.

Since C-V is five halves R, that is twenty point eight, f is five, a diatomic gas. By Mayer, C-P is C-V plus R, about twenty-nine point one, and gamma is that over C-V, seven fifths, one point four zero.
So a diatomic gas, with constant-pressure heat about twenty-nine point one joules per mole per kelvin and gamma one point four zero.
Now the speed trap. For which gas is the fraction of heat that becomes work the largest?
At constant pressure the work fraction is the work over the heat, which is n R over n C-P, that is R over C-P, equal to two over f plus two.

This decreases as f grows, so it is largest for the smallest f, the monoatomic gas: two fifths, forty percent. The trap is assuming polyatomic does the most work; instead its extra modes siphon heat away from expansion.
एक साफ़ identification, और एक N E E T-style trap इस बारे में कि कौन सी gas सबसे ज़्यादा expansion work करती है।
Board level. एक gas का constant-volume molar heat twenty point eight joules per mole per kelvin है। gas पहचानो, और उसका constant-pressure heat और gamma निकालो।
क्योंकि C-V है five halves R, यानी twenty point eight, f पाँच है, एक diatomic gas. Mayer से, C-P है C-V plus R, लगभग twenty-nine point one, और gamma है वो over C-V, seven fifths, one point four zero.
तो एक diatomic gas, constant-pressure heat लगभग twenty-nine point one joules per mole per kelvin और gamma one point four zero के साथ।
अब speed trap. किस gas के लिए heat का वो हिस्सा जो work बनता है सबसे बड़ा है?
constant pressure पर work fraction है work over heat, यानी n R over n C-P, यानी R over C-P, बराबर two over f plus two.

यह f बढ़ने पर घटता है, तो सबसे छोटे f के लिए सबसे बड़ा, monoatomic gas: two fifths, forty percent. trap है यह मानना कि polyatomic सबसे ज़्यादा work करती है; बजाय इसके उसके extra modes heat को expansion से खींच लेते हैं।

segments.text: A monoatomic gas heated two ways, showing exactly where the extra constant-pressure heat goes.
Two point zero moles of a monoatomic ideal gas are heated so the temperature rises by sixty kelvin. Find the heat at constant volume, at constant pressure, and the difference.
Monoatomic capacities: C-V is three halves R, about twelve point four seven; C-P is five halves R, about twenty point seven nine joules per mole per kelvin.
At constant volume the heat is n C-V times the temperature change: two times twelve point four seven times sixty, about one point five zero kilojoules.
At constant pressure it is n C-P times the temperature change: two times twenty point seven nine times sixty, about two point four nine kilojoules.
The difference between the two is the expansion work the gas does at constant pressure.
The difference is n R times the temperature change: two times eight point three one four times sixty, about nine hundred ninety-eight joules, roughly one point zero kilojoules.
That extra roughly one kilojoule at constant pressure is exactly the expansion work the gas does against the surroundings, the very R that appears in Mayer's relation.
एक monoatomic gas दो तरीक़ों से गरम, यह दिखाते हुए कि extra constant-pressure heat ठीक कहाँ जाती है।
two point zero moles monoatomic ideal gas को गरम किया जाता है ताकि temperature sixty kelvin बढ़े। constant volume पर, constant pressure पर heat, और difference निकालो।
monoatomic capacities: C-V है three halves R, लगभग twelve point four seven; C-P है five halves R, लगभग twenty point seven nine joules per mole per kelvin.
constant volume पर heat है n C-V into temperature change: two into twelve point four seven into sixty, लगभग one point five zero kilojoules.
constant pressure पर यह n C-P into temperature change: two into twenty point seven nine into sixty, लगभग two point four nine kilojoules.
दोनों के बीच का difference है वो expansion work जो gas constant pressure पर करती है।
difference है n R into temperature change: two into eight point three one four into sixty, लगभग nine hundred ninety-eight joules, मोटे तौर पर one point zero kilojoules.
वो extra लगभग एक kilojoule constant pressure पर ठीक वो expansion work है जो gas surroundings के against करती है, वही R जो Mayer's relation में आता है।
