board_events.text: Between $1.40$ and $1.67$, leaning diatomic (four to two)
Recipe: mole-weight, then Mayer, then ratio

segments.text: An advanced example: blend two gases and find the effective capacities and gamma.
A container holds two point zero moles of a monoatomic ideal gas and four point zero moles of a diatomic ideal gas. Find the mixture's constant-volume and constant-pressure capacities, and its gamma.
The mixture's gamma will land between the two pure components, pulled toward whichever dominates.
Mole-weight the constant-volume capacities: two times three halves R plus four times five halves R, all over six, which is thirteen sixths R, about two point one seven R.
By Mayer, the constant-pressure capacity is that plus R, which is nineteen sixths R.
So the mixture's gamma is nineteen sixths over thirteen sixths, which is nineteen over thirteen, about one point four six.
The mixture's gamma lies between the monoatomic one point six seven and the diatomic one point four zero, pulled toward the diatomic because diatomic moles dominate, four to two.
The recipe is general: mole-weight each capacity, apply Mayer for the constant-pressure value, then take the ratio for gamma.
एक advanced example: दो gases को मिलाओ और effective capacities और gamma निकालो।
एक container में two point zero moles monoatomic ideal gas और four point zero moles diatomic ideal gas है। mixture के constant-volume और constant-pressure capacities, और gamma निकालो।
mixture का gamma दोनों pure components के बीच गिरेगा, जो dominate करे उसकी तरफ़ खिंचा हुआ।
constant-volume capacities को mole-weight करो: two into three halves R plus four into five halves R, बटा six, यानी thirteen sixths R, लगभग two point one seven R.
Mayer से, constant-pressure capacity है वो plus R, यानी nineteen sixths R.
तो mixture का gamma है nineteen sixths over thirteen sixths, यानी nineteen over thirteen, लगभग one point four six.
mixture का gamma monoatomic one point six seven और diatomic one point four zero के बीच है, diatomic की तरफ़ खिंचा हुआ क्योंकि diatomic moles dominate करते हैं, four to two.
recipe general है: हर capacity को mole-weight करो, constant-pressure value के लिए Mayer लगाओ, फिर gamma के लिए ratio लो।

sections.title: Common pitfalls and pro-tips

board_events.text: Four traps, then the reflex identities
1. $\Delta U$ always rides $C_V$, never $C_P$
2. Diatomic $f=5$ at room temperature, not $7$
3. Specific is per kg; molar is per mole
4. Mayer is per mole and ideal-gas only
Reflex: $C_V=R/(\gamma-1)$, $C_P=\gamma R/(\gamma-1)$
Jump via $f$; work fraction $2/(f+2)$ cracks the traps

segments.text: Get the two capacities and gamma into reflex memory, and this hinge subtopic becomes automatic. Here are the traps.

Trap one, the most common. Using C-P for the internal-energy change. The internal-energy change is always n C-V times the temperature change, in every process; use C-P only for heat at constant pressure.
Trap two. Counting diatomic degrees of freedom as seven. At ordinary temperatures vibration is frozen, so f is five. Use seven only if a problem explicitly invokes high-temperature vibration.
Trap three. Mixing specific and molar capacities. Specific is per kilogram; molar is per mole; they differ by the molar mass.
Trap four. Forgetting that Mayer is per mole and ideal-gas only. C-P minus C-V equals R is not the relation for solids, liquids, or real gases except approximately.
Speed habit. Memorise the two reflex identities: C-V is R over gamma minus one, and C-P is gamma R over gamma minus one. They convert any gamma into capacities with no counting.

And jump via f for gas types: monoatomic three halves and five halves R; diatomic five halves and seven halves R; polyatomic three R and four R. The work fraction two over f plus two answers a whole class of traps.
दो capacities और gamma को reflex memory में डाल लो, और यह hinge subtopic automatic हो जाता है। यह रहे traps.
Trap एक, सबसे common. internal-energy change के लिए C-P use करना। internal-energy change हमेशा n C-V into temperature change है, हर process में; C-P सिर्फ़ constant pressure पर heat के लिए use करो।
Trap दो। diatomic degrees of freedom को सात गिनना। सामान्य temperatures पर vibration frozen है, तो f पाँच है। सात सिर्फ़ तब use करो जब problem साफ़-साफ़ high-temperature vibration की बात करे।
Trap तीन। specific और molar capacities को मिलाना। specific per kilogram है; molar per mole; वे molar mass से अलग होते हैं।
Trap चार। यह भूलना कि Mayer per mole और सिर्फ़ ideal-gas के लिए है। C-P minus C-V बराबर R, solids, liquids, या real gases के लिए relation नहीं है, सिवाय लगभग।
Speed habit. दो reflex identities याद रखो: C-V है R over gamma minus one, और C-P है gamma R over gamma minus one. वे किसी भी gamma को बिना गिने capacities में बदल देती हैं।

और gas types के लिए f से jump करो: monoatomic three halves और five halves R; diatomic five halves और seven halves R; polyatomic three R और four R. work fraction two over f plus two traps की एक पूरी class हल कर देता है।

board_events.text: Hot reservoir gives $Q_1$; cold reservoir takes $Q_2$
You can never convert all the heat into work
Over a cycle: $W=Q_1-Q_2$
Salary $Q_1$, take-home $W$, tax $Q_2$: the tax is never zero

segments.text: <excited>The first law says energy is conserved; it does not say energy is useful. A heat engine does the most economically important trick in physics.
It converts heat, the most disordered form of energy, into ordered mechanical work, over and over in a cycle. Every car engine, steam turbine, and power-plant boiler is a heat engine.
The picture is always the same three-part story.
A working substance draws heat Q one from a hot reservoir at temperature T one, converts part of it into work W, and dumps the leftover Q two into a cold reservoir at T two.
The phrase part of it is the whole drama. You can never convert all the heat into work; some must always be thrown away to the cold reservoir.
Because the substance returns to its starting state each cycle, its internal-energy change is zero, so the first law forces the work to equal Q one minus Q two.
Efficiency is the fraction of purchased heat that becomes useful work: the work over Q one, which is one minus Q two over Q one.
Think of Q one as your salary, W as the take-home you actually spend, and Q two as the tax siphoned off. Efficiency is the take-home fraction, and the tax can never be zero.
<excited>first law कहता है energy conserve होती है; यह नहीं कहता कि energy useful है। एक heat engine physics की सबसे economically ज़रूरी चाल करता है।
यह heat को, energy का सबसे disordered रूप, ordered mechanical work में बदलता है, बार-बार एक cycle में। हर car engine, steam turbine, और power-plant boiler एक heat engine है।
चित्र हमेशा वही तीन-हिस्सों की कहानी है।
एक working substance hot reservoir से temperature T one पर heat Q one खींचता है, उसका कुछ हिस्सा work W में बदलता है, और बचा हुआ Q two cold reservoir में T two पर डाल देता है।
वो phrase part of it ही पूरा drama है। आप कभी सारी heat को work में नहीं बदल सकते; कुछ हमेशा cold reservoir को फेंकना ही पड़ता है।
क्योंकि substance हर cycle अपनी शुरुआती state पर लौटता है, उसका internal-energy change zero है, तो first law work को Q one minus Q two के बराबर कर देता है।
efficiency है ख़रीदी heat का वो हिस्सा जो useful work बनता है: work over Q one, यानी one minus Q two over Q one.
Q one को अपनी salary सोचो, W को take-home जो आप सच में खर्च करते हो, और Q two को छाँटा गया tax. efficiency take-home fraction है, और tax कभी zero नहीं हो सकता।

board_events.text: Fridge pulls $Q_2$ from the cold food you store
Total $Q_1=Q_2+W$ goes to the warm side
Heat pump: same machine, but you want $Q_1$
COP = what you want over what you pay
COP can beat one: it is a ratio, not a percentage
A reservoir’s temperature does not change

segments.text: Now run the movie backwards. A refrigerator or heat pump is simply a heat engine running in reverse.
Instead of heat flowing naturally hot to cold and producing work, you supply work to force heat the unnatural way, cold to hot.
The fridge extracts heat Q two from the cold interior, your food. You pay work W, run by electricity in the compressor.
And the total, Q one equal to Q two plus W, is dumped into the warm kitchen, the coils at the back. That is why the room gets warmer than just the food's heat.
A heat pump is the identical machine, but now you care about the heat Q one delivered to the warm side, heating a house in winter. Same hardware, different goal.
So each has a different figure of merit, the coefficient of performance, defined as what you want divided by what you pay: Q two over W for a fridge, Q one over W for a pump.
And the coefficient of performance can exceed one, and usually does. It is not a percentage, so never cap it at one hundred percent.
One definition to keep clean: a reservoir is a body so large that its temperature does not change as heat is exchanged.
अब movie को उलटा चलाओ। एक refrigerator या heat pump बस एक heat engine है जो उलटा चल रहा है।
heat के hot से cold naturally बहकर work बनाने के बजाय, आप work देकर heat को उलटे रास्ते, cold से hot, मजबूर करते हो।
fridge cold interior, आपके खाने, से heat Q two खींचता है। आप work W चुकाते हो, compressor में बिजली से चलता।
और total, Q one बराबर Q two plus W, गरम kitchen में डाला जाता है, पीछे की coils. इसीलिए कमरा सिर्फ़ खाने की heat से ज़्यादा गरम होता है।
heat pump वही machine है, पर अब आप warm side को दी गई heat Q one की परवाह करते हो, सर्दियों में घर गरम करना। वही hardware, अलग goal.
तो हर एक का अलग figure of merit है, coefficient of performance, यानी जो आप चाहते हो बटा जो आप चुकाते हो: fridge के लिए Q two over W, pump के लिए Q one over W.
और coefficient of performance एक से ज़्यादा हो सकता है, और आमतौर पर होता है। यह percentage नहीं है, तो इसे कभी one hundred percent पर मत रोको।
एक definition साफ़ रखो: reservoir एक ऐसी body है जो इतनी बड़ी है कि heat exchange होने पर उसकी temperature नहीं बदलती।

board_events.text: $\eta=1$ breaks Kelvin-Planck; $\mathrm{COP}=\infty$ breaks Clausius

segments.text: Everything here flows from a single energy balance. Learn that one line and the rest is one division away.
The cyclic energy balance: Q one equals Q two plus W, because the internal-energy change over a cycle is zero.
Engine efficiency is the work over Q one, or one minus Q two over Q one, and it lies between zero and one, never reaching one.
The refrigerator's coefficient of performance is Q two over the work, which is Q two over Q one minus Q two.
The heat pump's coefficient is Q one over the work, which is Q one over Q one minus Q two.
Same hardware, opposite arrows: the engine and the refrigerator seen together.

Two relations tie it together. The pump coefficient is the fridge coefficient plus one. And the ideal Carnot limits use temperatures: max efficiency one minus T two over T one, and the coefficients T two or T one over T one minus T two.

And the second-law preview: an engine with efficiency one would violate the Kelvin-Planck statement; a fridge needing no work would violate the Clausius statement. That is why efficiency stays below one and the coefficient stays finite.
यहाँ सब कुछ एक energy balance से निकलता है। वो एक line सीखो और बाक़ी एक division दूर है।
cyclic energy balance: Q one बराबर Q two plus W, क्योंकि cycle में internal-energy change zero है।
engine efficiency है work over Q one, या one minus Q two over Q one, और यह zero और one के बीच रहती है, one तक कभी नहीं पहुँचती।
refrigerator का coefficient of performance है Q two over work, यानी Q two over Q one minus Q two.
heat pump का coefficient है Q one over work, यानी Q one over Q one minus Q two.
वही hardware, उलटे arrows: engine और refrigerator साथ देखे गए।

दो relations इसे जोड़ती हैं। pump coefficient है fridge coefficient plus one. और ideal Carnot limits temperatures use करती हैं: max efficiency one minus T two over T one, और coefficients T two या T one over T one minus T two.

और second-law preview: efficiency one वाला engine Kelvin-Planck statement तोड़ेगा; बिना work वाला fridge Clausius statement तोड़ेगा। इसीलिए efficiency one से नीचे रहती है और coefficient finite रहता है।

A COP above one is perfectly normal

segments.text: One straightforward engine, and one trap that catches students who put the wrong quantity in the denominator.
Start from the energy flow: heat in at the top, work out the side, heat rejected at the bottom.
Board level. In each cycle an engine absorbs one thousand joules from the hot reservoir and rejects six hundred joules to the cold reservoir. Find the work per cycle and the efficiency.
The work is Q one minus Q two, one thousand minus six hundred, four hundred joules. The efficiency is the work over Q one, four hundred over one thousand, forty percent.
Now the trap. A refrigerator extracts two hundred joules for every fifty joules of electrical work. Find its coefficient of performance and the heat dumped per cycle.
The coefficient is Q two over the work, two hundred over fifty, which is four. The heat dumped is Q two plus W, two hundred plus fifty, two hundred fifty joules.
The trap is computing Q two over Q one, two hundred over two hundred fifty, zero point eight, and calling it the coefficient. For a fridge the denominator is the work, not the hot-side heat.
And a coefficient of four, exceeding one, is perfectly normal. Never confuse it with an efficiency capped below one.
एक सीधा engine, और एक trap जो उन students को पकड़ता है जो denominator में ग़लत quantity डालते हैं।
energy flow से शुरू करो: ऊपर heat in, side से work out, नीचे heat rejected.
Board level. हर cycle में engine hot reservoir से one thousand joules absorb करता है और cold reservoir को six hundred joules reject करता है। work per cycle और efficiency निकालो।
work है Q one minus Q two, one thousand minus six hundred, four hundred joules. efficiency है work over Q one, four hundred over one thousand, forty percent.
अब trap. एक refrigerator हर fifty joules electrical work के लिए two hundred joules खींचता है। इसका coefficient of performance और per cycle dump हुई heat निकालो।
coefficient है Q two over work, two hundred over fifty, यानी four. dump हुई heat है Q two plus W, two hundred plus fifty, two hundred fifty joules.
trap है Q two over Q one, two hundred over two hundred fifty, zero point eight, निकालकर उसे coefficient कहना। fridge के लिए denominator work है, hot-side heat नहीं।
और four का coefficient, एक से ज़्यादा, बिलकुल सामान्य है। इसे one से नीचे capped efficiency से कभी मत confuse करो।

$200$ J of work moves $1000$ J: heat pumps beat heaters

segments.text: One inverse-efficiency numerical, and one ideal-device example that shows the leverage of a heat pump.
An engine has efficiency twenty-five percent and delivers five hundred joules of useful work per cycle. Find the heat absorbed and the heat rejected.

From efficiency equal to work over Q one, the heat absorbed is the work over the efficiency, five hundred over zero point two five, two thousand joules. The heat rejected is Q one minus W, one thousand five hundred joules.
A twenty-five percent engine throws away three-quarters of the heat it buys, a vivid reminder of why the rejected heat is never negligible.
Now an ideal Carnot device between a cold space and warm surroundings.
It operates between a cold space at two hundred fifty kelvin and surroundings at three hundred kelvin. Find its coefficient as a fridge, as a heat pump, and the work to remove one thousand joules.

For an ideal device the heat ratio equals the temperature ratio, so the fridge coefficient is T two over T one minus T two, two hundred fifty over fifty, five; the pump coefficient is T one over the same, three hundred over fifty, six; and five plus one is six.

The work to remove one thousand joules is Q two over the coefficient, one thousand over five, two hundred joules. That two hundred joules pumps one thousand joules out, and as a heat pump would deliver twelve hundred, which is exactly why heat pumps beat resistive heaters.
एक inverse-efficiency numerical, और एक ideal-device example जो heat pump का leverage दिखाता है।
एक engine की efficiency twenty-five percent है और per cycle five hundred joules useful work देता है। absorb हुई और reject हुई heat निकालो।

efficiency बराबर work over Q one से, absorb हुई heat है work over efficiency, five hundred over zero point two five, two thousand joules. reject हुई heat है Q one minus W, one thousand five hundred joules.
एक twenty-five percent engine जो heat ख़रीदता है उसका three-quarters फेंक देता है, एक साफ़ याद कि reject हुई heat कभी negligible नहीं होती।
अब cold space और warm surroundings के बीच एक ideal Carnot device.

यह cold space two hundred fifty kelvin पर और surroundings three hundred kelvin पर के बीच चलता है। इसका coefficient fridge के रूप में, heat pump के रूप में, और one thousand joules हटाने का work निकालो।

ideal device के लिए heat ratio बराबर temperature ratio, तो fridge coefficient है T two over T one minus T two, two hundred fifty over fifty, five; pump coefficient है T one over वही, three hundred over fifty, six; और five plus one बराबर six.

one thousand joules हटाने का work है Q two over coefficient, one thousand over five, two hundred joules. वो two hundred joules one thousand joules बाहर pump करता है, और heat pump के रूप में twelve hundred देगा, यही ठीक वजह है कि heat pumps resistive heaters को हराते हैं।

sections.title: Common pitfalls and pro-tips

board_events.text: Four traps, then the one-balance habit
1. The COP denominator is the work $W$
2. COP is a ratio, usually above one
3. Fridge: $Q_1=Q_2+W$, the room warms more
Start from $Q_1=Q_2+W$; the rest is one division
Ideal limits share $T_1-T_2$: small gap, great fridge

segments.text: Lock down the efficiency and the two coefficient formulas, and machines become bookkeeping. Here are the traps.
Trap one. Putting Q one in the coefficient denominator. For a fridge or pump the denominator is the work W, not the hot-side heat. It is Q two over W for a fridge, Q one over W for a pump.
Trap two. Treating the coefficient as a percentage capped at one hundred. It is a ratio that is normally greater than one; never write it as eighty percent.
Trap three. Forgetting Q one equals Q two plus W for a fridge. The hot-side heat is the cold-side heat plus the work you paid, so the room gets warmer than just the food's heat.
Trap four. Confusing efficiency with the rejected fraction. Efficiency is one minus Q two over Q one, not Q two over Q one itself.
Speed habit. Always start from the single balance, Q one equals Q two plus W. Everything else, efficiency or either coefficient, is one division away.
And for ideal limits, swap the heat ratio for the temperature ratio. Notice all three ideal formulas share the denominator T one minus T two: a small gap makes a great fridge but a feeble engine.
efficiency और दो coefficient formulas पक्की कर लो, और machines bookkeeping बन जाती हैं। यह रहे traps.
Trap एक। coefficient denominator में Q one डालना। fridge या pump के लिए denominator work W है, hot-side heat नहीं। यह fridge के लिए Q two over W, pump के लिए Q one over W है।
Trap दो। coefficient को one hundred पर capped percentage मानना। यह एक ratio है जो आमतौर पर एक से ज़्यादा है; इसे कभी eighty percent मत लिखो।
Trap तीन। fridge के लिए Q one बराबर Q two plus W भूलना। hot-side heat है cold-side heat plus आपका चुकाया work, तो कमरा सिर्फ़ खाने की heat से ज़्यादा गरम होता है।
Trap चार। efficiency को rejected fraction से confuse करना। efficiency है one minus Q two over Q one, ख़ुद Q two over Q one नहीं।
Speed habit. हमेशा एक balance से शुरू करो, Q one बराबर Q two plus W. बाक़ी सब, efficiency या कोई भी coefficient, एक division दूर है।
और ideal limits के लिए, heat ratio को temperature ratio से बदलो। ध्यान दो तीनों ideal formulas denominator T one minus T two share करती हैं: छोटा gap बढ़िया fridge बनाता है पर कमज़ोर engine.

board_events.text: Direction, not amount: what the first law cannot decide
One ordered arrangement, astronomically many disordered
Nature drifts toward the most probable, disordered states
Later quantified by a single number: entropy
The arrow is statistical, overwhelmingly certain

segments.text: <curious>The first law is generous to a fault. It would happily allow a cup of coffee to grow hotter while the room cools, because energy is still conserved. Yet you have never once seen it happen.

Watch any everyday process and you notice an arrow. Heat flows hot to cold, ink spreads through water, a swinging pendulum slows and stops. Each is energy-conserving in both directions, yet only one direction ever occurs.
The second law names this universal one-wayness: it tells us which way the movie of the universe is allowed to run.
Something beyond energy balance forbids the reverse. That something is the second law, and it is fundamentally about direction, not about amounts.
Picture shuffling a brand-new deck stacked in perfect order. A few shuffles and it is hopelessly mixed. There is exactly one ordered arrangement and astronomically many disordered ones.
Nature drifts toward the overwhelmingly more probable, disordered states. Heat spreading, ink diffusing, motion dissipating, all are the world shuffling toward its most probable condition.
The second law is the bookkeeping of that drift, and in the final subtopic we will quantify it with a single number called entropy.
One nuance. The arrow is statistical, overwhelmingly rather than metaphysically certain. It concerns macroscopic systems, where the odds against the reverse are simply astronomical.
<curious>first law हद से ज़्यादा उदार है। यह खुशी-खुशी कॉफ़ी को गरम होने देगा जबकि कमरा ठंडा हो, क्योंकि energy फिर भी conserve है। फिर भी आपने ऐसा एक बार भी होते नहीं देखा।

किसी भी रोज़मर्रा process को देखो और एक arrow दिखेगा। heat hot से cold बहती है, पानी में ink फैलती है, झूलता pendulum धीमा होकर रुक जाता है। हर एक दोनों directions में energy-conserving है, फिर भी सिर्फ़ एक direction होती है।
second law इस universal one-wayness को नाम देता है: यह बताता है कि universe की movie किस direction चलने की इजाज़त है।
energy balance से परे कोई चीज़ उलटी दिशा को रोकती है। वो चीज़ है second law, और यह मूल रूप से direction के बारे में है, amounts के बारे में नहीं।
एक बिलकुल नई deck सोचो जो perfect order में लगी है, उसे shuffle करो। कुछ shuffles में वो बुरी तरह मिल जाती है। ठीक एक ordered arrangement है और असंख्य disordered.
Nature भारी बहुमत से ज़्यादा probable, disordered states की तरफ़ बहती है। heat फैलना, ink फैलना, motion बिखरना, सब दुनिया का अपनी सबसे probable हालत की तरफ़ shuffle होना है।
second law उस drift का हिसाब है, और आख़िरी subtopic में हम इसे entropy नाम के एक single number से quantify करेंगे।
एक बारीक़ी। यह arrow statistical है, metaphysically के बजाय भारी बहुमत से certain. यह macroscopic systems की बात है, जहाँ उलटी दिशा के खिलाफ़ odds बस astronomical हैं।

board_events.text: Kelvin-Planck: no engine reaches efficiency one
Clausius: no free heat flow from cold to hot
The two statements are logically equivalent
Reversible: quasi-static, dissipation-free, retraceable
Irreversible: every real process leaves a permanent mark
Slow alone is not enough: dissipation must be absent too

segments.text: Historically the second law was stated two ways, born from two very practical frustrations.
Both statements are really bans on impossible machines.
Engineers building engines found they could never convert heat fully into work. The Kelvin-Planck statement captures this: no engine can have efficiency one.
Engineers building refrigerators found they could never move heat from cold to hot without paying work. The Clausius statement captures that.
Remarkably, these two no-free-lunch rules turn out to be logically equivalent. They are the same prohibition seen from the engine end and the fridge end.

A reversible process is an idealised limit: carried out infinitely slowly through a chain of equilibrium states, with no dissipation. Run it backwards and both system and surroundings retrace exactly.
Every irreversible process, which is to say every real one, generates entropy and cannot be undone without leaving a permanent mark on the surroundings.
One guardrail. Quasi-static alone is not enough. A slow process with friction is still irreversible. Reversibility needs both slowness and the absence of dissipation.
इतिहास में second law दो तरीक़ों से कहा गया, दो बहुत practical frustrations से जन्मा।
दोनों statements असल में impossible machines पर पाबंदियाँ हैं।
engines बनाने वाले engineers ने पाया कि वे heat को कभी पूरी तरह work में नहीं बदल पाते। Kelvin-Planck statement यही पकड़ता है: कोई engine efficiency one नहीं रख सकता।
refrigerators बनाने वाले engineers ने पाया कि वे heat को work चुकाए बिना कभी cold से hot नहीं ले जा पाते। Clausius statement यही पकड़ता है।
हैरानी की बात, ये दो no-free-lunch rules logically equivalent निकलती हैं। वे एक ही पाबंदी हैं, engine के छोर से और fridge के छोर से देखी गईं।
एक reversible process एक idealised limit है: बेहद धीरे, equilibrium states की एक chain से होकर, बिना किसी dissipation के। उलटा चलाओ और system और surroundings दोनों ठीक-ठीक अपने रास्ते वापस चलते हैं।
हर irreversible process, यानी हर असली process, entropy पैदा करती है और surroundings पर एक permanent mark छोड़े बिना undo नहीं हो सकती।
एक guardrail. सिर्फ़ quasi-static काफ़ी नहीं। friction वाली धीमी process अब भी irreversible है। reversibility को slowness और dissipation की गैरमौजूदगी दोनों चाहिए।

sections.subtopic: The Second Law of Thermodynamics & Reversibility
sections.title: Key statements and definitions

board_events.text: The two statements, and the two definitions
Kelvin-Planck: no full heat-to-work from a single reservoir
Clausius: no sole-effect heat from colder to hotter
A violation of either builds a violation of the other
Reversible: quasi-static, dissipation-free, no net change
Irreversible sources: friction, gap heat flow, free expansion, mixing
Forbidden only as a sole effect: a fridge is legal
They concern cyclic, macroscopic systems

segments.text: There is little algebra here; the power of this subtopic is in precise statements. Learn these word for word.

Kelvin-Planck statement, the engine form. No process is possible whose sole result is the complete conversion of heat absorbed from a single reservoir into work. Equivalently, no engine has efficiency one.
Clausius statement, the refrigerator form. No process is possible whose sole result is the transfer of heat from a colder body to a hotter body. Doing so always requires work input.
Equivalence. The two statements are logically identical: a violation of either can be used to construct a violation of the other, as the next section proves.
Reversible process. Carried out quasi-statically and free of all dissipation, such that reversing it restores both system and surroundings with no net change anywhere.

Irreversible process. Any process that cannot be reversed without a permanent change in the surroundings. Sources: finite-temperature-gap heat flow, friction, free expansion, mixing, and any sudden change.
A crucial nuance. Heat cold to hot is forbidden only as a sole effect. Supply work, and a refrigerator moves heat that way perfectly legally.
And these statements concern cyclic devices and macroscopic systems; the arrow they enforce is statistical, overwhelmingly certain.
यहाँ algebra कम है; इस subtopic की ताक़त precise statements में है। इन्हें शब्द-दर-शब्द सीखो।
Kelvin-Planck statement, engine form. कोई ऐसी process संभव नहीं जिसका sole result एक single reservoir से absorb की heat का पूरी तरह work में बदलना हो। यानी, कोई engine efficiency one नहीं रखता।
Clausius statement, refrigerator form. कोई ऐसी process संभव नहीं जिसका sole result किसी ठंडी body से गरम body में heat का transfer हो। ऐसा करने को हमेशा work input चाहिए।
Equivalence. दोनों statements logically identical हैं: किसी एक का violation दूसरे का violation बनाने में use हो सकता है, जैसा अगला section साबित करता है।
Reversible process. quasi-statically और सभी dissipation से मुक्त की गई, ऐसी कि उलटने पर system और surroundings दोनों बिना किसी net change के बहाल हो जाएँ।
Irreversible process. कोई भी process जो surroundings में permanent change के बिना उलटी न हो सके। Sources: finite-temperature-gap heat flow, friction, free expansion, mixing, और कोई भी अचानक change.
एक ज़रूरी बारीक़ी। heat का cold से hot सिर्फ़ sole effect के रूप में मना है। work दो, और एक refrigerator उस तरह heat पूरी तरह legally ले जाता है।
और ये statements cyclic devices और macroscopic systems की बात करती हैं; जो arrow वे लागू करती हैं वो statistical है, भारी बहुमत से certain.

board_events.text: Engine: draws $Q_1$, does $Q_1-Q_2$, rejects $Q_2$
Cold reservoir nets zero heat
Heat from one reservoir, fully to work: Kelvin-Planck broken
A Kelvin-Planck violator builds a Clausius violator too
One prohibition, two faces: equivalent

segments.text: The cleanest way to prove the two statements are the same is to show that violating one lets you violate the other. This is the JEE-Advanced classic.
Suppose a magic device C moves heat from the cold reservoir to the hot reservoir with no work input, violating Clausius.
Now run an ordinary engine between the same two reservoirs. It draws Q one from the hot side, does work equal to Q one minus Q two, and rejects exactly Q two to the cold side.
Combine the magic device and the engine into one composite. On the cold reservoir the net heat change is zero: the engine rejected Q two, and the device carried exactly that Q two back.
So the sole net result of the composite is heat, Q one minus Q two, drawn from the hot reservoir alone, converted entirely into work, with no other effect. That is a Kelvin-Planck violation.
The reverse direction works just as cleanly. Feed a Kelvin-Planck violator's work into an ordinary refrigerator, and the composite moves heat cold to hot with no work, a Clausius violation.
So the two statements stand or fall together. Break one and you can always rig a machine that breaks the other; they are one prohibition wearing two faces.
दोनों statements के एक होने का सबसे साफ़ सबूत यह दिखाना है कि एक का violation दूसरे का violation करा देता है। यह J E E-Advanced का classic है।
मान लो एक magic device C बिना work input के cold reservoir से hot reservoir में heat ले जाता है, Clausius को तोड़ते हुए।
अब उन्हीं दो reservoirs के बीच एक ordinary engine चलाओ। यह hot side से Q one खींचता है, Q one minus Q two जितना work करता है, और ठीक Q two cold side को reject करता है।
magic device और engine को एक composite में मिलाओ। cold reservoir पर net heat change zero है: engine ने Q two reject किया, और device ने ठीक वही Q two वापस ले लिया।
तो composite का sole net result है heat, Q one minus Q two, अकेले hot reservoir से खींची, पूरी तरह work में बदली, बिना किसी और असर के। यही Kelvin-Planck violation है।
उलटी दिशा भी उतनी ही साफ़ चलती है। एक Kelvin-Planck violator का work एक ordinary refrigerator में डालो, और composite बिना work के heat cold से hot ले जाता है, एक Clausius violation.
तो दोनों statements साथ खड़े रहते या गिरते हैं। एक तोड़ो और आप हमेशा दूसरे को तोड़ने वाली machine बना सकते हैं; वे एक ही पाबंदी हैं, दो चेहरों में।

board_events.text: Sudden, gap heat flow, and friction all fail
Only the frictionless quasi-static isothermal is reversible
Slow is necessary, not sufficient

segments.text: One board-style statement question, and one NEET trap that catches the word slow.
Board level. State the Kelvin-Planck and Clausius statements, and give one everyday process that shows the natural direction the law enforces.
Kelvin-Planck: no engine can, in a cycle, take heat from a single reservoir and convert it entirely into work. Clausius: heat cannot flow on its own from a colder to a hotter body.

Everyday illustration. A hot cup of tea always cools to room temperature, giving heat to the cooler room. It never spontaneously draws heat from the cool room to grow hotter, exactly the Clausius direction.
Now the trap. Which of these is reversible: free expansion into vacuum, heat across a large gap, a frictionless quasi-static isothermal expansion, or a block sliding to rest by friction?
Reversible needs quasi-static and dissipation-free. Free expansion is sudden, so not quasi-static. A finite temperature gap and friction are both dissipative.
So only the frictionless quasi-static isothermal expansion, in contact with a reservoir at the gas's own temperature, qualifies as reversible.
The trap is equating slow with reversible. Slowness, being quasi-static, is necessary but not sufficient; a slow process with friction is still irreversible.
एक board-style statement सवाल, और एक N E E T trap जो slow शब्द पर पकड़ता है।
Board level. Kelvin-Planck और Clausius statements बताओ, और एक रोज़मर्रा process दो जो law की लागू की natural direction दिखाए।
Kelvin-Planck: कोई engine एक cycle में single reservoir से heat लेकर उसे पूरी तरह work में नहीं बदल सकता। Clausius: heat अपने आप ठंडी से गरम body में नहीं बह सकती।
रोज़मर्रा illustration. गरम चाय हमेशा room temperature तक ठंडी होती है, ठंडे कमरे को heat देते हुए। यह कभी अपने आप ठंडे कमरे से heat खींचकर गरम नहीं होती, ठीक Clausius direction.
अब trap. इनमें reversible कौन है: vacuum में free expansion, बड़े gap के पार heat, एक frictionless quasi-static isothermal expansion, या friction से रुकता block?
reversible को quasi-static और dissipation-free चाहिए। free expansion अचानक है, तो quasi-static नहीं। finite temperature gap और friction दोनों dissipative हैं।
तो सिर्फ़ frictionless quasi-static isothermal expansion, gas के अपने temperature के reservoir के contact में, reversible के तौर पर qualify करती है।
trap है slow को reversible के बराबर मानना। slowness, यानी quasi-static, ज़रूरी है पर काफ़ी नहीं; friction वाली धीमी process अब भी irreversible है।

$150$ J to pure work: Clausius holds forces Kelvin-Planck

segments.text: One device to judge, and one concrete-number version of the equivalence proof.

Main level. An inventor claims a cyclic engine that, each cycle, absorbs five hundred joules from a reservoir at four hundred kelvin and produces five hundred joules of work, rejecting no heat. First law, second law, both, or neither?
First-law check. Energy in is five hundred joules, energy out as work is five hundred joules, and the cyclic internal-energy change is zero. Energy balances, so the first law is satisfied.
Second-law check. The sole result is complete conversion of heat from a single reservoir into work, with nothing rejected, precisely the Kelvin-Planck prohibition. It violates the second law only.
Advanced level. Show that a device moving one hundred joules from cold to hot with no work, combined with an ordinary engine, manufactures a Kelvin-Planck violator.

Let the engine draw two hundred fifty joules from the hot reservoir, do work equal to two hundred fifty minus one hundred, that is one hundred fifty joules, and reject one hundred joules to the cold reservoir.
The magic device carries that same one hundred joules back from cold to hot, free of charge. The cold reservoir nets minus one hundred plus one hundred, which is zero.
The composite's sole effect: one hundred fifty joules drawn from the hot reservoir alone, fully converted to work. A Kelvin-Planck violation, so Clausius holding forces Kelvin-Planck to hold.
एक device जाँचनी है, और equivalence proof का एक concrete-number version.

Main level. एक inventor एक cyclic engine का दावा करता है जो हर cycle four hundred kelvin के reservoir से five hundred joules absorb करता है और five hundred joules work बनाता है, कोई heat reject किए बिना। first law, second law, दोनों, या कोई नहीं?
first-law check. energy in है five hundred joules, work बनकर energy out है five hundred joules, और cyclic internal-energy change zero है। energy balance है, तो first law satisfied.
second-law check. sole result है single reservoir से heat का पूरी तरह work में बदलना, कुछ भी reject किए बिना, ठीक Kelvin-Planck prohibition. यह सिर्फ़ second law तोड़ता है।
Advanced level. दिखाओ कि एक device जो बिना work के one hundred joules cold से hot ले जाती है, एक ordinary engine के साथ मिलकर एक Kelvin-Planck violator बना देती है।
engine को hot reservoir से two hundred fifty joules खींचने दो, two hundred fifty minus one hundred, यानी one hundred fifty joules work करने दो, और cold reservoir को one hundred joules reject करने दो।
magic device वही one hundred joules cold से hot वापस ले जाता है, मुफ़्त में। cold reservoir पर net है minus one hundred plus one hundred, यानी zero.
composite का sole effect: one hundred fifty joules अकेले hot reservoir से खींची, पूरी तरह work में बदली। एक Kelvin-Planck violation, तो Clausius का टिकना Kelvin-Planck को टिकने पर मजबूर करता है।

sections.subtopic: The Second Law of Thermodynamics & Reversibility
sections.title: Common pitfalls and pro-tips

board_events.text: Four traps, then the sole-effect habit
1. Slow is not enough; dissipation kills reversibility
2. Cold to hot is banned only as a sole effect
3. Kelvin-Planck is engines; Clausius is fridges
4. A violator still conserves energy
Reduce to the sole net effect over one cycle
Assume one violation, bolt on a device, read the other

segments.text: This is the conceptual bridge to the Carnot engine, so keep the ideas crisp. Here are the traps.
Trap one. Slow equals reversible. Quasi-static is necessary but not sufficient; dissipation, whether friction or finite-gap heat flow, makes even a slow process irreversible.
Trap two. Thinking the second law bans heat cold to hot outright. It bans it only as a sole effect; with work input, a refrigerator does exactly that, perfectly legally.
Trap three. Confusing the two statements. Kelvin-Planck is the engine, heat to work, prohibition; Clausius is the refrigerator, heat cold to hot, prohibition.
Trap four. Believing a Kelvin-Planck violator breaks the first law. It does not; energy is conserved. The whole point is that the second law forbids things the first law permits.

Speed habit. In any is-this-device-possible question, reduce it to its sole net effect over one cycle. Heat from one reservoir to pure work is a Kelvin-Planck violation; heat cold to hot with no work is a Clausius violation.
And remember the direction of the equivalence proof: assume one violation, bolt on an ordinary engine or fridge, cancel the cold-reservoir heat, and read off the other violation.
यह Carnot engine तक का conceptual पुल है, तो ideas साफ़ रखो। यह रहे traps.
Trap एक। slow बराबर reversible। quasi-static ज़रूरी है पर काफ़ी नहीं; dissipation, चाहे friction हो या finite-gap heat flow, धीमी process को भी irreversible बना देता है।
Trap दो। यह सोचना कि second law heat के cold से hot को पूरी तरह मना करता है। यह इसे सिर्फ़ sole effect के रूप में मना करता है; work input के साथ, refrigerator ठीक वही करता है, पूरी तरह legally.
Trap तीन। दोनों statements को confuse करना। Kelvin-Planck engine, heat to work, की पाबंदी है; Clausius refrigerator, heat cold से hot, की पाबंदी है।
Trap चार। यह मानना कि Kelvin-Planck violator first law तोड़ता है। नहीं तोड़ता; energy conserve है। पूरी बात यही है कि second law उन चीज़ों को मना करता है जिन्हें first law इजाज़त देता है।

Speed habit. किसी भी is-this-device-possible सवाल में, इसे एक cycle के sole net effect तक घटा दो। एक reservoir से heat pure work में Kelvin-Planck violation है; बिना work के heat cold से hot Clausius violation.
और equivalence proof की दिशा याद रखो: एक violation मान लो, एक ordinary engine या fridge जोड़ो, cold-reservoir heat cancel करो, और दूसरा violation पढ़ लो।

board_events.text: Built from isothermal and adiabatic reversible steps
Every irreversibility is wasted, capturable work
The reversible ideal sits at the second law’s boundary
A real plant reaches a fraction of the Carnot ceiling

segments.text: <curious>The second law told us efficiency must be less than one. But how close to one can we get? In eighteen twenty-four a young French engineer, Sadi Carnot, asked the deepest version of that question.
Of all conceivable engines working between a hot reservoir at T one and a cold one at T two, which is the best, and what limits it?

His answer is one of the most beautiful results in physics: the best engine is fully reversible, its efficiency depends only on the two temperatures, and that efficiency is one minus T two over T one.
The Carnot engine is the idealised, perfectly reversible engine that achieves this ceiling.
Its cycle is built from the two reversible ways to move a gas we already mastered: isothermal steps, in contact with a reservoir, and adiabatic steps, perfectly insulated.

Why insist on reversibility? Because every irreversibility, friction, a finite temperature gap, turbulence, is wasted opportunity, energy degraded into useless heat you could otherwise have captured as work.
A reversible engine wastes nothing; it operates at the exact boundary the second law allows. It is the frictionless, lossless ideal, the perfect yardstick.
So a real power plant quoting forty-two percent efficient is really saying it reached forty-two percent of the way to the Carnot ceiling set by its boiler and cooling-tower temperatures.

<curious>second law ने बताया कि efficiency one से कम होनी चाहिए। पर हम one के कितने पास पहुँच सकते हैं? eighteen twenty-four में एक नौजवान French engineer, Sadi Carnot ने उस सवाल का सबसे गहरा रूप पूछा।
T one पर hot reservoir और T two पर cold के बीच काम करते सभी सोचे-समझे engines में, सबसे अच्छा कौन है, और उसे क्या सीमित करता है?

उसका जवाब physics के सबसे खूबसूरत नतीजों में से एक है: सबसे अच्छा engine पूरी तरह reversible है, उसकी efficiency सिर्फ़ दो temperatures पर depend करती है, और वो efficiency है one minus T two over T one.
Carnot engine वो idealised, perfectly reversible engine है जो यह ceiling हासिल करता है।
इसका cycle gas को हिलाने के उन दो reversible तरीक़ों से बना है जिन पर हमारी पकड़ है: isothermal steps, reservoir के contact में, और adiabatic steps, perfectly insulated.
reversibility पर ज़ोर क्यों? क्योंकि हर irreversibility, friction, finite temperature gap, turbulence, एक गँवाया मौक़ा है, energy बेकार heat में degrade, जिसे आप वरना work के रूप में पकड़ सकते थे।
एक reversible engine कुछ नहीं गँवाता; यह ठीक उस boundary पर चलता है जो second law इजाज़त देता है। यह frictionless, lossless ideal है, perfect yardstick.
तो forty-two percent efficient बताता real power plant असल में कह रहा है कि वो अपने boiler और cooling-tower temperatures की तय की Carnot ceiling तक forty-two percent पहुँचा।

board_events.text: 1. Isothermal expansion at $T_1$: absorb $Q_1$
2. Adiabatic expansion: cools from $T_1$ to $T_2$
3. Isothermal compression at $T_2$: reject $Q_2$
4. Adiabatic compression: warms $T_2$ back to $T_1$
Net work = enclosed area = $Q_1-Q_2$
Heat only on the two isotherms; adiabatics exchange none

segments.text: The cycle runs through four reversible steps and returns the gas exactly to its start.
Follow the loop clockwise: expand hot, expand insulated, compress cold, compress insulated.
Stroke one, isothermal expansion at T one. Touching the hot reservoir, the gas expands slowly and absorbs heat Q one. Since the internal energy does not change here, that heat equals the work done.
Stroke two, adiabatic expansion. Insulated now, the gas expands further, doing work at the cost of its internal energy, cooling from T one to T two.
Stroke three, isothermal compression at T two. Touching the cold reservoir, the gas is compressed slowly, rejecting heat Q two.
Stroke four, adiabatic compression. Insulated again, the gas is compressed back to its starting state, warming from T two to T one.
The net work per cycle is the area enclosed by this loop on the P-V diagram, and as always the work equals Q one minus Q two.
And notice: heat enters only on stroke one and leaves only on stroke three. The two adiabatic strokes exchange no heat at all.
cycle चार reversible steps से गुज़रता है और gas को ठीक उसकी शुरुआत पर लौटा देता है।
loop को clockwise follow करो: गरम में फैलो, insulated फैलो, ठंडे में compress, insulated compress.
Stroke एक, T one पर isothermal expansion. hot reservoir को छूते हुए, gas धीरे फैलती है और heat Q one absorb करती है। चूँकि यहाँ internal energy नहीं बदलती, वो heat किए work के बराबर है।
Stroke दो, adiabatic expansion. अब insulated, gas और फैलती है, अपनी internal energy की क़ीमत पर work करते हुए, T one से T two तक ठंडी होते हुए।
Stroke तीन, T two पर isothermal compression. cold reservoir को छूते हुए, gas धीरे compress होती है, heat Q two reject करते हुए।
Stroke चार, adiabatic compression. फिर insulated, gas अपनी शुरुआती state पर वापस compress होती है, T two से T one तक गरम होते हुए।
हर cycle का net work P-V diagram पर इस loop से घिरा area है, और हमेशा की तरह work बराबर Q one minus Q two.
और ध्यान दो: heat सिर्फ़ stroke one पर आती है और सिर्फ़ stroke three पर जाती है। दोनों adiabatic strokes बिलकुल heat exchange नहीं करते।

board_events.text: No engine beats reversible; all reversible engines tie
Efficiency depends only on the two temperatures

segments.text: The formula sheet, and the theorem that makes efficiency a property of temperatures alone.
Heat is exchanged only on the isotherms. The gas absorbs n R T one times the log of V B over V A, and rejects n R T two times the log of V C over V D.
The key ratio, derived from the adiabatic relations, is Q two over Q one equals T two over T one, with temperatures in kelvin.
So the Carnot efficiency is one minus Q two over Q one, which is one minus T two over T one, or T one minus T two over T one.
The same cycle reversed gives the Carnot refrigerator and heat pump.
Reversed, the coefficients are T two over T one minus T two for the fridge, and T one over the same denominator for the pump.

Carnot's theorem. First, no engine between two reservoirs can beat a reversible one between the same two. Second, all reversible engines between the same reservoirs tie, regardless of working substance.
The consequence is that efficiency depends only on T one and T two. This substance-independence is what lets us define an absolute, thermodynamic temperature scale.
formula sheet, और वो theorem जो efficiency को सिर्फ़ temperatures की property बनाता है।
heat सिर्फ़ isotherms पर exchange होती है। gas n R T one into log of V B over V A absorb करती है, और n R T two into log of V C over V D reject करती है।
key ratio, adiabatic relations से निकला, है Q two over Q one बराबर T two over T one, temperatures kelvin में।
तो Carnot efficiency है one minus Q two over Q one, यानी one minus T two over T one, या T one minus T two over T one.
वही cycle उलटा Carnot refrigerator और heat pump देता है।
उलटा, coefficients हैं fridge के लिए T two over T one minus T two, और pump के लिए T one over वही denominator.

Carnot's theorem. पहला, दो reservoirs के बीच कोई engine उन्हीं दो के बीच एक reversible engine को नहीं हरा सकता। दूसरा, उन्हीं reservoirs के बीच सभी reversible engines बराबर होते हैं, working substance चाहे जो हो।
नतीजा यह कि efficiency सिर्फ़ T one और T two पर depend करती है। यही substance-independence हमें एक absolute, thermodynamic temperature scale define करने देती है।

board_events.text: The substance cancels: only $T_1$ and $T_2$ remain

segments.text: Work the four steps with an ideal gas and watch the working substance vanish from the answer.
Label the corners A, B, C, D around the loop.
Step one, heat on the two isotherms. On the hot isotherm Q one is n R T one times the log of V B over V A; on the cold one Q two is n R T two times the log of V C over V D.
Step two, apply the adiabatic relation to the two insulated steps, using T V to the gamma minus one is constant.
Step three, divide one by the other to eliminate the temperatures. The result rearranges to a clean volume identity: V B over V A equals V C over V D.
Step four, take the ratio of the two heats. The two logarithms are now equal and cancel, leaving Q two over Q one equals T two over T one.
Substitute into the efficiency to get the crown result: Carnot efficiency is one minus T two over T one.
The working substance has vanished from the answer, a preview of Carnot's theorem: no gas, no size, no amount survives, only the two temperatures.
चार steps को ideal gas के साथ चलाओ और देखो कि working substance answer से गायब हो जाता है।
loop के चारों कोनों को A, B, C, D नाम दो।
Step one, दो isotherms पर heat. hot isotherm पर Q one है n R T one into log of V B over V A; cold पर Q two है n R T two into log of V C over V D.
Step two, दो insulated steps पर adiabatic relation लगाओ, T V to the gamma minus one constant use करते हुए।
Step three, temperatures हटाने को एक को दूसरे से भाग दो। नतीजा एक साफ़ volume identity में बदल जाता है: V B over V A बराबर V C over V D.
Step four, दोनों heats का ratio लो। दोनों logarithms अब बराबर हैं और cancel हो जाते हैं, छोड़ते हुए Q two over Q one बराबर T two over T one.
efficiency में substitute करके crown नतीजा पाओ: Carnot efficiency है one minus T two over T one.
working substance answer से गायब हो गया, Carnot's theorem की झलक: कोई gas, कोई size, कोई amount नहीं बचता, सिर्फ़ दो temperatures.

board_events.text: Claim one: assume $\eta_X$ exceeds $\eta_R$
X needs less hot heat than R returns
A Clausius violation, so $\eta_X\le\eta_R$
Claim two: two reversible engines must be equal
All reversible tie, so $\eta$ depends on temperatures alone
It defines absolute temperature via the heat ratio

segments.text: Two claims, both proved by the same trick: assume the opposite and build a second-law violation.
Suppose an engine X between the two reservoirs were more efficient than a reversible engine R.
Claim one. No engine X can beat a reversible engine R between the same reservoirs. Suppose it could; run R backwards as a refrigerator, driven by X's work.
Because X is more efficient, it needs less heat from the hot reservoir than R pumps back into it. The net effect is heat delivered cold to hot with no external work.
That is a Clausius violation, so the assumption fails. Hence the efficiency of X is at most the efficiency of R: no engine beats the reversible one.

Claim two. Two reversible engines must tie. Apply the argument once with the first driving the second reversed, then again the other way; each gives one efficiency at most the other, so they are equal.
So all reversible engines tie regardless of working substance. Efficiency can therefore depend only on the two reservoir temperatures, which is exactly what one minus T two over T one says.
This substance-independence is also what lets us define an absolute, thermodynamic temperature scale through the heat ratio Q two over Q one equals T two over T one.
दो claims, दोनों एक ही चाल से साबित: उल्टा मान लो और एक second-law violation बना दो।
मान लो दो reservoirs के बीच एक engine X एक reversible engine R से ज़्यादा efficient होता।
Claim एक। उन्हीं reservoirs के बीच कोई engine X एक reversible engine R को नहीं हरा सकता। मान लो हरा सकता; R को refrigerator की तरह उलटा चलाओ, X के work से चलाया हुआ।
क्योंकि X ज़्यादा efficient है, इसे hot reservoir से उतनी heat नहीं चाहिए जितनी R वापस pump करता है। net effect है heat का cold से hot पहुँचना बिना किसी external work के।
यह एक Clausius violation है, तो assumption गिर जाता है। इसलिए X की efficiency ज़्यादा से ज़्यादा R की efficiency है: कोई engine reversible को नहीं हराता।
Claim दो। दो reversible engines बराबर होने चाहिए। argument एक बार लगाओ पहले को दूसरे उलटे को चलाते हुए, फिर उल्टा; हर बार एक efficiency ज़्यादा से ज़्यादा दूसरी, तो वे बराबर हैं।
तो सभी reversible engines working substance चाहे जो हो, बराबर होते हैं। इसलिए efficiency सिर्फ़ दो reservoir temperatures पर depend कर सकती है, ठीक वही जो one minus T two over T one कहता है।
यही substance-independence हमें heat ratio Q two over Q one बराबर T two over T one के ज़रिए एक absolute, thermodynamic temperature scale define करने देती है।

segments.text: One direct efficiency, and one that tests whether you invert the formula cleanly.
Efficiency is set by the two temperatures alone, and lowering the sink helps more than raising the source.
Board level. A Carnot engine operates between a hot reservoir at five hundred kelvin and a cold reservoir at three hundred kelvin. Find its efficiency.
Efficiency is one minus T two over T one, one minus three hundred over five hundred, one minus zero point six, which is zero point four zero, forty percent. No detail of the gas is needed.

Speed trap. A Carnot engine has efficiency fifty percent with the cold reservoir at three hundred kelvin. To raise the efficiency to sixty percent keeping the cold fixed, by how much must the hot temperature rise?

Invert the formula: T one is T two over one minus efficiency. At fifty percent, T one is three hundred over zero point five, six hundred kelvin. At sixty percent, it is three hundred over zero point four, seven hundred fifty kelvin.

So the hot temperature must rise from six hundred to seven hundred fifty kelvin, an increase of one hundred fifty kelvin. The trap is scaling temperature linearly with efficiency; always invert cleanly.
एक direct efficiency, और एक जो जाँचता है कि आप formula को साफ़-साफ़ invert करते हो या नहीं।
efficiency सिर्फ़ दो temperatures से तय होती है, और sink को नीचे लाना source को ऊपर करने से ज़्यादा मदद करता है।
Board level. एक Carnot engine five hundred kelvin के hot reservoir और three hundred kelvin के cold reservoir के बीच चलता है। इसकी efficiency निकालो।
efficiency है one minus T two over T one, one minus three hundred over five hundred, one minus zero point six, यानी zero point four zero, forty percent. gas की कोई detail नहीं चाहिए।
Speed trap. एक Carnot engine की efficiency fifty percent है, cold reservoir three hundred kelvin पर। cold fixed रखते हुए efficiency sixty percent करने को, hot temperature कितना बढ़नी चाहिए?

formula invert करो: T one है T two over one minus efficiency. fifty percent पर, T one है three hundred over zero point five, six hundred kelvin. sixty percent पर, यह three hundred over zero point four, seven hundred fifty kelvin.
तो hot temperature six hundred से seven hundred fifty kelvin बढ़नी चाहिए, one hundred fifty kelvin की बढ़त। trap है temperature को efficiency के साथ linearly scale करना; हमेशा साफ़ invert करो।

segments.text: One multi-part numerical, and one that is the pure essence of Carnot's theorem.
Main level. A Carnot engine between four hundred kelvin and three hundred kelvin absorbs twelve hundred joules per cycle. Find the efficiency, the work, and the heat rejected.

Efficiency is one minus three hundred over four hundred, twenty-five percent. Work is efficiency times Q one, zero point two five times twelve hundred, three hundred joules. Heat rejected is Q one minus work, nine hundred joules.
Now the ceiling question. An inventor claims a certain efficiency between six hundred and three hundred kelvin.

Advanced level. A reversible engine runs between six hundred kelvin and three hundred kelvin. Find the Carnot efficiency; is a claimed sixty percent possible; and if the claim were forty-five percent, is that possible and necessarily reversible?
The Carnot efficiency is one minus three hundred over six hundred, fifty percent.

The claimed sixty percent exceeds the ceiling, so by Carnot's theorem it is impossible; it would enable a Clausius violation. Forty-five percent is below the ceiling, so it is possible, but being below the maximum it must be irreversible; only a reversible engine reaches the full fifty percent.
This three-part question is the essence of Carnot's theorem: the reversible efficiency is simultaneously the maximum and the value all reversible engines share.
एक multi-part numerical, और एक जो Carnot's theorem का शुद्ध सार है।
Main level. four hundred kelvin और three hundred kelvin के बीच एक Carnot engine हर cycle twelve hundred joules absorb करता है। efficiency, work, और reject हुई heat निकालो।

efficiency है one minus three hundred over four hundred, twenty-five percent. work है efficiency into Q one, zero point two five into twelve hundred, three hundred joules. reject हुई heat है Q one minus work, nine hundred joules.
अब ceiling सवाल। एक inventor six hundred और three hundred kelvin के बीच एक efficiency का दावा करता है।

Advanced level. एक reversible engine six hundred kelvin और three hundred kelvin के बीच चलता है। Carnot efficiency निकालो; क्या दावा किया sixty percent संभव है; और अगर दावा forty-five percent हो, क्या वो संभव और ज़रूरी reversible है?
Carnot efficiency है one minus three hundred over six hundred, fifty percent.

दावा किया sixty percent ceiling से ऊपर है, तो Carnot's theorem से यह असंभव है; यह एक Clausius violation करा देगा। forty-five percent ceiling से नीचे है, तो संभव है, पर maximum से नीचे होने से यह irreversible होना चाहिए; सिर्फ़ reversible engine पूरे fifty percent तक पहुँचता है।
यह तीन-हिस्सों वाला सवाल Carnot's theorem का सार है: reversible efficiency एक साथ maximum है और वो value जो सभी reversible engines share करते हैं।

sections.title: Common pitfalls and pro-tips

board_events.text: Four traps, then the one-line engine
1. The efficiency formula is valid only in kelvin
2. Heat only on the isotherms; adiabatics exchange none
3. Carnot is a ceiling; real engines fall below
4. Lowering the sink beats raising the source
Two isos, two adias, heat on the isos, $\eta=1-T_2/T_1$
Efficiency first; a claim above the ceiling is impossible

segments.text: This is the crown of the chapter, the absolute speed limit on every engine. Here are the traps.
Trap one. Forgetting to convert to kelvin. Efficiency equals one minus T two over T one is valid only in kelvin; plugging in Celsius gives nonsense, sometimes even an efficiency above one.
Trap two. Thinking heat is exchanged on all four steps. Only the two isotherms exchange heat; the adiabatic steps are insulated, so their heat is zero.
Trap three. Believing a real engine can reach Carnot efficiency. Carnot is the reversible ceiling; every real, irreversible engine falls strictly below it.
Trap four. Confusing raise T one with lower T two. For equal temperature changes, lowering the sink T two raises efficiency more than raising the source T one.
Speed habit. Memorise the engine in one line: two isotherms, two adiabats, heat only on the isotherms, efficiency one minus T two over T one in kelvin.

And for any numerical, get efficiency from the temperatures first, then work equals efficiency times Q one, and heat rejected is Q one minus work. If a claimed efficiency exceeds one minus T two over T one, declare it impossible on the spot.
यह chapter का ताज है, हर engine पर absolute speed limit. यह रहे traps.
Trap एक। kelvin में convert करना भूलना। efficiency बराबर one minus T two over T one सिर्फ़ kelvin में सही है; Celsius डालना बकवास देता है, कभी-कभी तो one से ज़्यादा efficiency.
Trap दो। यह सोचना कि heat चारों steps पर exchange होती है। सिर्फ़ दो isotherms heat exchange करते हैं; adiabatic steps insulated हैं, तो उनकी heat zero है।
Trap तीन। यह मानना कि real engine Carnot efficiency तक पहुँच सकता है। Carnot reversible ceiling है; हर real, irreversible engine इससे strictly नीचे रहता है।
Trap चार। raise T one को lower T two से confuse करना। बराबर temperature changes के लिए, sink T two को नीचे लाना source T one को ऊपर करने से efficiency ज़्यादा बढ़ाता है।
Speed habit. engine को एक line में याद रखो: दो isotherms, दो adiabats, heat सिर्फ़ isotherms पर, efficiency one minus T two over T one kelvin में।

और किसी भी numerical में, पहले temperatures से efficiency निकालो, फिर work बराबर efficiency into Q one, और reject हुई heat है Q one minus work. अगर दावा की efficiency one minus T two over T one से ज़्यादा हो, वहीं impossible घोषित कर दो।

board_events.text: The universe’s entropy change is at least zero
Entropy is the scorecard for how shuffled things are
A freezer orders water but disorders the room more
The ratio $dQ/T$ is the heartbeat of entropy

segments.text: <curious>The previous subtopic gave the second law in words: real processes have a preferred direction. But direction begged for a number, one that always increases. That number is entropy.
The cleanest reading of entropy is the amount of disorder, or more precisely the number of microscopic arrangements, the microstates, consistent with the bulk state.

Heat Q flowing into a system at temperature T raises its disorder by Q over T. And the colder the system, the bigger the disordering effect, like a whisper in a silent library versus the same whisper at a loud party.
So the total entropy of the universe never decreases, even when a system's own entropy falls.
The second law now wears a number: the entropy change of the universe is at least zero, for every real process.

Recall the shuffled-deck image. Entropy is the precise scorecard for how shuffled. A perfectly ordered deck has low entropy; a thoroughly mixed one has high entropy, and every real process shuffles the universe a little more.

You can lower a system's entropy, a freezer makes ordered ice from disordered water, but only by dumping even more disorder into the surroundings, as the coils warm the kitchen. The universe's entropy still rises.
That single ratio, dQ over T, is the heartbeat of entropy, and everything in this subtopic flows from it.
<curious>पिछले subtopic ने second law शब्दों में दिया: असली processes की एक preferred direction होती है। पर direction को एक number चाहिए था, जो हमेशा बढ़े। वो number है entropy.
entropy का सबसे साफ़ मतलब है disorder की मात्रा, या ज़्यादा ठीक-ठीक microscopic arrangements की संख्या, microstates, जो bulk state के साथ मेल खाती हैं।

temperature T पर system में बहती heat Q उसके disorder को Q over T बढ़ाती है। और system जितना ठंडा, उसी heat का disordering असर उतना बड़ा, जैसे शांत library में एक whisper बनाम loud party में वही whisper.
तो universe की कुल entropy कभी नहीं घटती, तब भी जब किसी system की अपनी entropy गिरे।
second law अब एक number पहनता है: universe का entropy change कम से कम zero है, हर असली process के लिए।

shuffle की गई deck की image याद करो। entropy ठीक-ठीक scorecard है कि कितना shuffled. perfectly ordered deck की entropy कम; अच्छी तरह मिली की ज़्यादा, और हर असली process universe को थोड़ा और shuffle करती है।

आप किसी system की entropy घटा सकते हो, freezer disordered पानी से ordered बर्फ़ बनाता है, पर सिर्फ़ surroundings में और ज़्यादा disorder डालकर, जैसे coils kitchen गरम करती हैं। universe की entropy फिर भी बढ़ती है।
वो एक ratio, dQ over T, entropy की धड़कन है, और इस subtopic में सब कुछ इसी से निकलता है।

board_events.text: $dS=dQ_{rev}/T$ is path-independent along reversible routes
Irreversible? Route through any reversible path with the same ends
Use the reversible heat and the kelvin temperature
System entropy alone may be positive, negative, or zero
Only the universe total, system plus surroundings, cannot fall
Zero only for reversible; strictly positive for real processes

segments.text: Entropy is a state function; it depends only on the state, not the path. But heat is a path function. How do we rescue a state function out of a path quantity?
The trick is to insist on the reversible path.
Along any reversible route between two states, the integral of the reversible heat over temperature comes out the same. So it legitimately defines the entropy change, dS equals dQ reversible over T.
So to find the entropy change of an irreversible process, cleverly compute it along any reversible path with the same endpoints. Because entropy is a state function, the answer is identical.
One guardrail. The definition needs the reversible heat and the temperature at which it is exchanged, in kelvin, always.
The entropy change of the system alone can be positive, negative, or zero. A system's entropy may legitimately fall, during freezing or compression.
It is the entropy change of the universe, system plus surroundings, that obeys the rule of never decreasing.
And equality, an entropy change of exactly zero, holds only for a reversible process. Every irreversible, real process gives a strictly positive universe entropy change.
entropy एक state function है; यह सिर्फ़ state पर depend करती है, path पर नहीं। पर heat एक path function है। हम एक path quantity से एक state function कैसे बचाएँ?
चाल है reversible path पर ज़ोर देना।
दो states के बीच किसी भी reversible रास्ते पर, reversible heat over temperature का integral एक ही निकलता है। तो यह सही से entropy change define करता है, dS बराबर dQ reversible over T.
तो किसी irreversible process का entropy change निकालने को, चतुराई से इसे उन्हीं endpoints वाले किसी reversible path पर compute करो। entropy state function होने से, answer वही रहता है।
एक guardrail. definition को reversible heat और वो temperature चाहिए जिस पर वो exchange होती है, kelvin में, हमेशा।
अकेले system का entropy change positive, negative, या zero हो सकता है। किसी system की entropy सही में गिर सकती है, freezing या compression के दौरान।
यह universe का entropy change है, system plus surroundings, जो कभी न घटने का नियम मानता है।
और equality, ठीक zero का entropy change, सिर्फ़ reversible process के लिए होता है। हर irreversible, असली process universe का strictly positive entropy change देता है।

segments.text: The compact sheet: the definition, the entropy form of the second law, and the standard results.

For a reversible exchange of heat at absolute temperature T, dS is dQ reversible over T; the entropy change is the integral. Entropy is a state function, so its cyclic integral is zero, and its unit is joules per kelvin.
The entropy form of the second law: the entropy change of the universe, system plus surroundings, is at least zero, with equality only for a reversible process.
The Clausius inequality, for any cyclic process using the actual heat: the cyclic integral of dQ over T is at most zero, zero if reversible, negative if irreversible.
Here are the standard entropy changes worth memorising.

Isothermal for an ideal gas is n R times the log of final over initial volume; a phase change is m L over T; heating at constant pressure is n C-P times the log of final over initial temperature; a reversible adiabatic is zero.
The general ideal-gas form combines a temperature change and a volume change: n C-V times the log of the temperature ratio plus n R times the log of the volume ratio.
For an irreversible process, compute the system's entropy change along a reversible path, and the surroundings' change as minus the actual heat over the surroundings' temperature. Then add.
compact sheet: definition, second law का entropy रूप, और standard नतीजे।

absolute temperature T पर heat के reversible exchange के लिए, dS है dQ reversible over T; entropy change integral है। entropy state function है, तो इसका cyclic integral zero है, और unit joules per kelvin.
second law का entropy रूप: universe का entropy change, system plus surroundings, कम से कम zero है, equality सिर्फ़ reversible process के लिए।
Clausius inequality, किसी भी cyclic process के लिए actual heat use करते हुए: dQ over T का cyclic integral ज़्यादा से ज़्यादा zero है, reversible हो तो zero, irreversible हो तो negative.
यह रहे standard entropy changes जो याद रखने लायक़ हैं।

ideal gas के लिए isothermal है n R into log of final over initial volume; phase change है m L over T; constant pressure पर heating है n C-P into log of final over initial temperature; reversible adiabatic zero है।
general ideal-gas रूप temperature change और volume change दोनों जोड़ता है: n C-V into log of temperature ratio plus n R into log of volume ratio.
किसी irreversible process के लिए, system का entropy change reversible path पर निकालो, और surroundings का change minus actual heat over surroundings' temperature. फिर जोड़ो।

board_events.text: $2.0$ mol, isothermal reversible at $400$ K, volume doubles
Reversible, so the universe change is zero
$0.5$ kg ice melts; $L=3.34\times10^5$ J per kg
Melting frees a rigid lattice: a large positive change

segments.text: Two clean single-formula entropy changes, both coming out positive as disorder grows.
A gas spreading into a larger volume and ice melting to water both raise entropy.
Main level. Two point zero moles of an ideal gas expand isothermally and reversibly at four hundred kelvin to twice their initial volume. Find the entropy change of the gas.
Isothermal, so the entropy change is n R times the log of the volume ratio: two times eight point three one four times the natural log of two, about eleven point five joules per kelvin.
Positive, as expected: the gas spreads into a larger volume, more disorder. And since the process is reversible, the surroundings lose exactly eleven point five, so the universe change is zero.

Advanced level. Zero point five kilograms of ice melts completely to water at zero degrees Celsius. The latent heat of fusion is three point three four times ten to the fifth joules per kilogram. Find the entropy change.

A phase change at constant temperature, two hundred seventy-three kelvin, so the entropy change is m L over T: zero point five times three point three four times ten to the fifth, over two hundred seventy-three, about six hundred twelve joules per kelvin.
Melting injects heat at constant temperature, sharply raising disorder as the rigid lattice dissolves into a free-flowing liquid, a large positive entropy change.
दो साफ़ single-formula entropy changes, दोनों positive निकलते हैं जैसे disorder बढ़ता है।
बड़े volume में फैलती gas और पानी में पिघलती बर्फ़ दोनों entropy बढ़ाती हैं।
Main level. two point zero moles ideal gas four hundred kelvin पr isothermally और reversibly अपने initial volume के दुगुने तक फैलती है। gas का entropy change निकालो।
isothermal, तो entropy change है n R into log of volume ratio: two into eight point three one four into natural log of two, लगभग eleven point five joules per kelvin.
positive, जैसा उम्मीद थी: gas बड़े volume में फैलती है, ज़्यादा disorder. और process reversible होने से, surroundings ठीक eleven point five खोती हैं, तो universe change zero है।

Advanced level. zero point five kilograms बर्फ़ zero degrees Celsius पr पूरी तरह पानी में पिघलती है। latent heat of fusion है three point three four into ten to the fifth joules per kilogram. entropy change निकालो।

constant temperature पr phase change, two hundred seventy-three kelvin, तो entropy change है m L over T: zero point five into three point three four into ten to the fifth, over two hundred seventy-three, लगभग six hundred twelve joules per kelvin.
melting constant temperature पr heat डालती है, disorder को तेज़ी से बढ़ाते हुए जैसे rigid lattice एक free-flowing liquid में घुलती है, एक बड़ा positive entropy change.
